src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.
tgt: Seemo sa Kabinete mo mererong e e kwa setlhoeng mo maemong a ga jaanong.

src: Cabinet expressed concern at recent labour unrest at Lonmin’s Marikana Mine which has led to the downing of tools and a disruption of productivity.
tgt: Kabinete e tlhagisitse matshwenyego a yona tebang le dikhuduego tsa fa gautshwane tse di bakileng go ngala tiro le go kgoreletsa tlhagiso kwa Moepong wa Lonmin kwa Marikana.

src: The dispute is reported as centering around issues of majority representation involving the National Union of Mineworkers and the Association for Mining and Construction Union.
tgt: Go begwa fa mooko wa kgotlhang e le ntlha ya kemedi e kgolo go gaisa e e akaretsang Mokgatlho wa Bosetšhaba wa Badiramoepong (NUM) le Mokgatlho wa Meepo le Boagi (AMCU).Kabinete e ikuela kwa boeteledipeleng jwa mekgatlho ka bobedi (NUM le AMCU) go rarabolola dikgotlhang tsa bona ka kagiso le go baya dikgatlhegelo tsa naga le badiri godimo ga tsotlhe.

src: Cabinet appeals to the leadership of both unions (NUM and AMCU) to resolve their dispute amicably and put the interests of the country and workers above everything else.
tgt: Badiri ba tshwanetse go lemoga gore mogwanto yo o sa sireletsegang o ka nna le ditlamorago tse di bosula mo badiring le mo isagong ya meepo le ditiro tsa bone.

src: Cabinet also appeals to Lonmin management to do everything possible to make sure that the problems are resolved as soon as possible without further damage.
tgt: Gape Kabinete e ikuela kwa botsamaising jwa Lonmin go dira tsotlhe tse di kgonegang go netefatsa gore mathata a rarabololwa ka bonako jo bo ka kgonegang kwa ntle ga ditshenyegelo tse dingwe.

src: It is in the best interest of the country for both unions and management at Lonmin to demonstrate required levels of leadership and industrial relations management.
tgt: Go mo dikgatlhegong tsa naga le mekgatlho ka bobedi mmogo le botsamaisi jwa Lonmin go supa boeteledipele jo bo tlhokegang le tsamaiso ya dikamano tsa badiri.

src: Cabinet fully supports the preliminary findings from the investigation into the unauthorised landing of a civilian aircraft at Waterkloof Air Force Base.
tgt: Kabinete e tshegetsa ka botlalo diphitlhelelo tsa pulamadibogo tsa patlisiso ya go tsuruma go go sa letlelelwang ga sefofane sa banamedi kwa Boemelafofaneng jwa Sesole jwa Waterkloof.

src: Cabinet stressed that the safety and sovereignty of South Africa is of paramount importance.
tgt: Kabinete e gateletse gore pabalesego le go ikemela ga Aforika Borwa go botlhokwa thata.

src: Violation of laws and rules relevant to the ports of entry and facilities of strategic national importance must be dealt with firmly and without fear or favour.
tgt: Go tshwanetse ga samaganwa le kgatako ya melao le melawana e e malebana le matseno le ditlamelo tsa botlhokwa tsa setšhaba ka tsepamo, kwa ntle ga letshogo gongwe go direla yo mongwe molemo.

src: Those who are found to infringe and compromise regulations must face the full might of the law.
tgt: Ba go fitlhelwang ba tlola gongwe ba nyatsa melawana ba tshwanetse go lebagana le bogale jotlhe jwa molao.

src: Cabinet welcomes the work by Government Departments which has been reported on by various Ministers during the departmental Budget Votes.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela tiro ya Mafapha a Puso e e begilweng ke Ditona tse di farologaneng ka nako ya Ditekanyetsokabo tsa mafapha.

src: Cabinet notes that the coverage afforded to the Budget Votes assists in empowering citizens with information and holding government accountable.
tgt: Kabinete e lemoga gore go begwa ga Ditekanyetsokabo go thusa go maatlafatsa baagi ka tshedimosetso le go rwesa puso maikarabelo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the discussions between the Department of Basic Education and the South African Democratic Teachers' Union (SADTU) which led to the suspension of protest action.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela dipuisano tse di lebisitseng kwa go sekegiweng ga dikgato tsa ngongorego magareng ga Lefapha la Thuto ya Motheo le Mokgatlho wa Temokerasi wa Barutabana wa Aforika BorwaKabinete e ikuela mo batsayakarolong botlhe mo lephateng la thuto go rarabolola dikgotlhang tsa bone gore thuto ya bana e se ke ya amega.

src: Cabinet noted the Quarterly Labour Force Survey (QLFS) which shows an increase in the unemployment rate from 24,9 per cent to 25,2 per cent.
tgt: Kabinete e itemogetse Tshekatsheko ya Kotara ya Palo ya Badiri e e bontshang koketsego ya seelo sa botlhokatiro go tloga go diphesente di le 24,9 go ya go diphesente di le 25,2.Puso e akofisa dikgato di tshwana le letsholo le le eteletsweng pele ke mmuso la mafaratlhatlha, go oketsa ditiro ka ditsereganyo tsa Lephata la Setšhaba.

src: Government is accelerating measures, such as the state-led infrastructure drive, to increase employment through Public Sector interventions.
tgt: Puso mmogo le lephata la badiri le kgwebo, ba tlhomile Tumelano ya Loago ya Go Thapiwa ga Bašwa ka Moranang 2013.

src: This further demonstrates a collective commitment towards addressing the issue of unemployment.
tgt: Seno se bontsha gape maitlamo a a tlhakanetsweng malebana le go samagana le ntlha ya botlhokatiro.

src: It maps out individual sector pledges to contribute in fighting youth unemployment with concrete targets and time frames for successful execution, monitoring and collective evaluation of the identified interventions.
tgt: E tlhalosa maikano a maphata a a farologaneng tebang le go tsayakarolo mo go lwantsheng botlhokatiro jwa bašwa ka dipeelo tse di tsepameng le nako e e beilweng go lebeletswe tiragatso, tlhokomelo mmogo le tshekatsheko e e tlhakanetsweng ya ditsereganyo tse di supilweng.

src: Cabinet remains confident that measures already underway will assist the country to create new jobs and realise its target of five-million new jobs by 2020.
tgt: Kabinete e na le bonnete jwa gore dikgato tse di setseng di tsentswe tirisong di tla thusa naga go tlhama ditiro tse dintšhwa le go fitlhelela diphitlhelelo tse di totilweng tsa ditiro tse dintšhwa di le dimilione di le tlhano ka 2020.

src: Cabinet welcomes the signing of an action plan to implement the Memorandum of Understanding on Biodiversity Conservation and Protection between South Africa and Vietnam.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela go saeniwa ga leano la tiragatso go tsenya tirisong Memorantamo wa Ditumelano o o ka ga Tshomarelo le Tshireletso ya Ditshedi tse di Farologaneng magareng ga Aforika Borwa le Vietnam.

src: The Implementation Plan will run until 2017 and will assist efforts to combat crime involving wildlife, particularly rhino poaching.
tgt: Leano la Tiragatso le tla dira go fitlha ka 2017 mme le tla thusa maiteko a go lwantsha bosenyi jo bo amang diphologolo tsa naga, bogolo segolo bogodu jwa go tumola dinaka tsa ditshukudu.

src: Cabinet reiterates that Government is committed to addressing the scourge of rhino poaching and reaffirms that perpetrators will be prosecuted.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa gore Puso e itlamile go samagana le leroborobo la bogodu jwa go tumola dinaka tsa ditshukudu mme e boa e itlama gore ba ba molato ba tla sekisiwa.

src: Cabinet welcomes the announcement by the Department of Home Affairs to pilot the Smart ID card system, which further consolidates our national identity and enhances national security.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela kitsiso ya Lefapha la Merero ya Selegae go lekeletsa Thulaganyo ya karata ya Boitshupo, e e gokaganyang boitshupo jwa rona jwa bosetšhaba mme e tokafatse tshireletsego ya bosetšhaba.

src: This key milestone holds the potential to speed up government services, while cutting down on crime and corruption involving identity documents.
tgt: Go na le kgonagalo ya gore phitlhelelo eno ya botlhokwa e ka akofisa ditirelo tsa puso, fa e tla bo e fokotsa bosenyi le bobodu jo bo amanang le makwaloitshupo.

src: Cabinet calls on South Africans to support this process so that by 2020 we are all in receipt of a Smart ID Card as a form of national identification.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo maAforika Borweng go tshegetsa tsamaiso eno gore ka 2020 rotlhe re bo re amogetse Karata ya Boitshupo jaaka karolo ya boitshupo jwa bosetšhaba.

src: Cabinet condemns the attack on a United Nations convoy in Abyei, Sudan, which resulted in the deaths of a tribal chief and an Ethiopian peacekeeper.
tgt: Kabinete e nyatsa tlhaselo e e bakileng dintsho tsa kgosi ya morafe le modiri wa kagiso wa Itopia mo mokolokong wa Ditšhabakopano kwa Abyei, Sudan.

src: This regrettable incident threatens the stability of Abyei as well as the progress recently achieved by Sudan and South Sudan.
tgt: Tiragalo eno e e swabisang e tshosetsa go tsepama ga Abyei gammogo le tswelelopele e e sa tswang go fitlhelelwa ke Sudan le Sudan o o kwa Borwa.

src: Cabinet denounces the attack on Syria by the Israeli security forces.
tgt: Kabinete e nyatsa tlhaselo ya Seria e e dirilweng ke masole a tshireletso a Iseraele.

src: Cabinet calls on the United Nations to prevail on external forces to respect the sovereignty of Syria and to allow Syrians to work together in resolving their disputes.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela go Ditšhabakopano go netefatsa gore maphata a kwa ntle a tlotla go ikemela ga Seria le go letla maSeria go dira mmogo go rarabolola dikgotlhang tsa ona.

src: Cabinet welcomed the inauguration of Advocate Lawrence Mushwana as the new Chairperson of the International Co-ordinating Committee (ICC) of National Institutions for the Promotion and Protection of Human Rights.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse go tlhomiwa ga Moatefokate Lawrence Mushwana jaaka Modulasetilo o montšhwa wa Komiti ya Boditšhabatšhaba ya Kgokaganyo (ICC) ya Ditheo tsa Bosetšhaba tsa Tsweletso le Tshireletso ya Ditshwanelo tsa Botho.

src: This is the first time that Africa heads the office of the Chairperson of the ICThe position of ICC Chairperson secures increased focus on the country's human rights track record and its compliance with international human rights obligations.
tgt: Ke la ntlha Aforika e etelela pele kantoro ya Modulasetilo wa ICMaemo a Modulasetilo wa ICC a netefatsa tebo e e oketsegileng mo rekotong ya ditshwanelo tsa botho ya naga gammogo le kobamelo ya yona ya maitlamo a boditšhabatšhaba a ditshwanelo tsa botho.

src: Cabinet welcomed that the 50th anniversary of the Organisation of African Unity which will be celebrated on Africa Day, 25 May 2013.Cabinet highlighted that the solidarity of the OAU in excluding the apartheid government from its organs uplifted our struggle for freedom and attainment of democracy.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse segopotso sa bo 50 sa Mokgatlho wa Tshwaragano ya Aforika (OAU) se se tla ketikiwang ka Letsatsi la Aforika, la bo 25 Motsheganong 2013.

src: South Africa will join the continent in commemorating the 50th Anniversary of the African Union.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla golagana le kontinete go keteka Segopotso sa bo 50 sa Tshwaragano ya Aforika.

src: The activities include a month-long exhibition of contemporary visual arts in the SADC region from 24 May to 28 June 2013.
tgt: Ditiragalo di akaretsa dipontsho tsa kgwedi yotlhe tsa botsweretshipono mo kgaolong ya SADC go tloga ka la bo 24 Motsheganong go fitlha ka la bo 28 Seetebosigo 2013.

src: The Africa Institute of South Africa will also convene the academic community and diaspora as part of the commemorations on 19-21 May 2013.
tgt: Setheo sa tsa Aforika sa Aforika Borwa se tla kokoanya barutegi le ba ditšhaba jaaka karolo ya segopotso ka la bo 19-21 Motsheganong 2013.

src: Furthermore, there will be an exhibition at the Ditsong Museum (City of Tshwane) to commemorate Africa Day on 21 May 2013 under the theme “50 Years after forming the Organisation of African Union – Africa must unite or Perish”.
tgt: Godimo ga moo, go tla nna le dipontsho kwa Musiamong wa Ditsong (Motsemogolo wa Tshwane) go keteka Letsatsi la Aforika ka la bo 21 Motsheganong 2013 ka moono wa "Dingwaga tse 50 morago ga go tlhamiwa ga OAU - Aforika e tshwanetse go tshwaragana kgotsa e nyelele."

src: This will be followed by a Africa Day music concert at the Union Buildings on 25 May 2013.
tgt: Seno se tla latelwa ke konsarata ya mmino ya Letsatsi la Aforika kwa Union Buildings ka la bo 25 Motsheganong 2013.

src: Cabinet welcomed President Jacob Zuma’s speedy response to the invitation by a community member to visit the people of Eldorado Park and neighbouring Kliptown, on Tuesday, 14 May 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse tsibogelo ya ka bonako ya Moporesitente Jacob Zuma mo taletsong ya moagi gore a etele batho ba kwa Eldorado Park le ba kwa Kliptown e e gaufi, ka Labobedi, la bo 14 Motsheganong 2013.

src: The community’s request was to discuss the escalating illegal drug trafficking and abuse problem in the area.
tgt: Kopo ya baagi e ne e le malebana le go buisanela go gola ga kgwebo e e seng mo molaong ya diritibatsi le bothata jwa tiriso ya tsone e e botlhaswa mo tikologong eo.

src: Government, together with the community, has committed to accelerate the intervention programme to stop the scourge that is destroying young people.
tgt: Puso, mmogo le baagi, ba itlamile go akofisa lenaneo la tsereganyo go emisa leroborobo le le bolayang bašwa.

src: Cabinet welcomed the follow up visit by Deputy President Motlanthe, accompanied by leaders of the three spheres of government, to De Doorns in the Western Cape on Saturday 11 May 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse ketelo ya tatediso ya Motlatsamoporesitente Motlanthe, a patilwe ke baeteledipele ba magato a le mararo a puso, go ya kwa De Doorns kwa Kapa Bophirima ka Lamatlhatso, la bo 11 Motsheganong 2013.

src: The visit and dialogue with stakeholders including farmworkers stems from the initial visit of the Deputy President on 12 February 2013.
tgt: Ketelo le dipuisano le baamegi ba ba akaretsang badiri ba dipolase e latela ketelo ya ntlha ya Motlatsamoporesitente ka la bo 12 Tlhakole 2013.

src: Solid progress was noted from a number of departments in improving services in the area.
tgt: Go lemogilwe tswelelopele e e tsepameng ya go tokafatsa ditirelo mo tikolong eo go tswa mo mafapheng a le mmalwa.

src: The commitment demonstrated by all parties lays a solid foundation for ongoing engagement toward a sustainable agrarian sector.
tgt: Maitlamo a a bontshitsweng ke maphata otlhe ke motheo wa dipuisano tse di tswelelang go lebeletswe gore go nne le lephata la leruri la temothuo.

src: Key Cabinet discussions and decisions.
tgt: Dipuisano le ditshweetso tsa botlhokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet was briefed on preparations for Child Protection Week (CPW) between 27 May and 2 June 2013, under the theme: “Working together to protect children.”	The child and youth dialogues are being conducted in all provinces as a build up to the launch of Child Protection Week and the Conference.
tgt: Kabinete e itsisitswe ka dithulaganyo tsa Beke ya Tshireletso ya Bana (CPW) magareng ga 27 Motsheganong le 2 Seetebosigo 2013 ka moono wa "Re dira mmogo go sireletsa bana.

src: As part of awareness-raising, Child Protection Week will be launched together with the orphans, vulnerable children and youth (OVCY) Conference on 27 May at the Inkosi Albert Luthuli International Convention Centre in KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: "Go tsweletswe ka dipuisano tsa bana le bašwa mo diporofenseng tsotlhe go baakanyetsa go tlhomiwa ga CPW le Khonferense.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to contribute towards the protection of our children and create a safe and secure environment.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo maAforika Borweng otlhe go tshayakarolo mo tshireletsong ya bana ba rona le go tlhama tikologo e e babalesegileng e bile e sireletsegile.

src: South Africans can visibly demonstrate their support by wearing a green ribbon as a symbol of life, growth, hope, care and support for our future leaders.
tgt: MaAforika Borwa a ka bontsha tshegetso ya ona ka go apara lente le le tala jaaka letshwao la go supa botshelo, kgolo, tsholofelo, tlhokomelo le tshegetso ya baeteledipele ba rona ba isago.

src: The focus of Child Protection Week and the Orphans, Vulnerable Children and Youth Conference is on child participation in our society and communities so that children are heard on matters affecting them.
tgt: CPW le OVYC di lebeletse seabe sa baagi gore bana ba reediwe malebana le merero e e ba amang.

src: Cabinet approved the National Aquaculture Policy Framework (NAPF).
tgt: Kabinete e rebotse Letlhomeso la Pholisi ya Bosetšhaba ya Boruatlhapi (NAPF).

src: This policy provides a unified framework for the establishment and development of an industry that contributes towards sustainable job creation and increased investment.
tgt: Pholisi eno e tlamela ka letlhomeso le le kopaneng la go tlhamiwa le go tlhabololwa ga intaseteri e e tsayang karolo mo go tlhamiweng ga ditiro tsa leruri mmogo le dipeeletso tse di oketsegileng.

src: The NAPF was developed against the backdrop of a global aquaculture sector that has seen an increased demand for fishery products.
tgt: NAPF e tlhamilwe go lebeletswe lephata la boruatlhapi le le itemogetseng koketsego ya go batlega ga dikuno tsa ditlhapi.

src: In South Africa, marine and freshwater aquaculture presents a good opportunity to diversify fish production to satisfy local demand, contribute to food security, job creation, economic development and rural development, and export opportunities.
tgt: Mo Aforika Borwa, boruatlhapi jwa mo lewatleng le mo metsing a a foreše bo tlamela ka tšhono e e siameng ya go atolosa tlhagiso ya ditlhapi go kgotsofatsa tlhokego ya selegae, go tsayakarolo mo tlhagisong e e sa tlhaeleng ya dijo, go tlhama ditiro, go tlhabolola ikonomi mmogo le go tlhabolola metseselegae, gammogo le ditšhono tsa thomelontle.

src: Cabinet approved that South Africa hosts the Third Global Conference on Agriculture, Food Security and Climate Change in the fourth quarter of 2013, led by the Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries.
tgt: Kabinete e rebotse gore Aforika Borwa, e eteletswe pele ke Lefapha la Temothuo, Jalo ya Dikgwa le Bodirelatlhapi, e amogele Khonferense ya Boraro ya Lefatshe ya Temothuo, Tlhagiso e e sa Tlhaeleng ya Dijo le Phetogo ya Tlelaemete mo kotareng ya bone ya 2013.Tlhagiso e e sa tlhaeleng ya dijo e sa ntse e le ntlha e e tshwenyang go gaisa mme Khonferense e tla nna le ditlamorago tse di siameng tebang le ka moo re tlhagisang, re tsamaisang le go dirisa dijo ka gona.

src: Food security remains a major concern and the Conference will have positive implications for how we produce, manage and utilise food.
tgt: Fa e sa le ka COP17/MP7, Aforika Borwa e ntse e le nngwe ya dinaga tse di eteletseng pele mo go tsweletseng temothuo e e botlhale e e tsibogelang dikgwetlho tsa go nna teng ga dijo mmogo le phetogo ya tlelaemete.

src: Since COP17/CMP7, South Africa has been one of the leading countries in promoting climate smart agriculture, which responds to the challenges of food security and climate change.
tgt: Maikaelelo a Khonferense ya Lefatshe ke go tlhama mekgwa ya kgolo e e ka dirisegang go ya go ile mo loagong le mo tikologong.

src: Cabinet approved South Africa’s ratification of the Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) Annex to the Southern African Development Community’s Protocol on Trade and for this to be submitted to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse tlhomamiso ya Aforika Borwa ya Mametlelelo ya Tlhokomelo ya Ditshedi le Tlhokomelo ya Dijalo (SPS) mo Mametlelelong ya Molao wa Kgwebisano ya Dinaga tsa Mokgatlho wa Tlhabololo ya Borwa jwa Aforika (SADC) le gore e isiwe kwa Palamenteng.

src: The SADC Protocol on Trade to which South Africa has acceded serves to promote regional cooperation and integration amongst member states for trade in goods and services within the region, including agricultural products.
tgt: Molao wa Kgwebisano ya SADC e Aforika Borwa e dumelaneng nayo e tsweletsa tirisanommogo ya kgaolo le kgolagano magareng ga dinaga tse e leng ditokololo malebana le kgwebisano ya dithoto le ditirelo mo kgaolong, go akarediwa dikumo tsa temothuo.

src: The SADC SPS Annex to the SADC Protocol on Trade provides an enabling framework for SPS cooperation.
tgt: Mametlelelo ya SADC SPC ya Molao wa Kgwebisano ya SADC e tlamela ka letlhomeso le le kgontshang tirisanommogo ya SPGape e tsweletsa kgokaganyo ya dikgato tsa SPS tse di ikaegileng ka seemo le kaedi ya boditšhabatšhaba go gokaganya kgwebisano e e babalesegileng le e e sa gobeleleng ya dikuno tsa temothuo mo kgaolong.

src: It also promotes harmonisation of SPS measures based on international standards and guidelines in order to facilitate safe and fair trade of agriculture products in the region.
tgt: Kabinete e sedimoseditswe ka tswelelopele e e amanang le go amogela Dikopano tsa Aforika Borwa ka ga Sekema sa Ditifikeiti tsa Tiragatso sa Kimberley (KPCS), go simolola ka la bo 4 go fitlha ka la bo 7 Seetebosigo le Kopano ya KPCS kwa Gauteng go tloga ka la bo 26 go fitlha ka la bo 29 Ngwanaitseele 2013.

src: Cabinet was updated on progress relating to South Africa’s hosting of the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme (KPCS) meetings in 2013, which includes the Inter-sessional meeting in Kimberley from 4 to 7 June and the KPCS Plenary in Gauteng from 26 to 29 November 2013.
tgt: Go amogelwa ga dikopano tsa KPCS go tla tsayakarolo mo tsweletsong ya intaseteri ya ditaemane le bojanala.

src: South Africa’s position as chair of the KPCS gives recognition to the key role that South Africa plays in the international diamond sector.
tgt: Maemo a Aforika Borwa jaaka modulasetilo wa KPCS a lemoga seabe se segolo se Aforika Borwa e nang naso mo lephateng la boditšhabatšhaba la ditaemane.

src: As the chair South Africa aims to strengthen international trade relations, with a view to consolidate and increase the African footprint within the KPCS and contribute to a safer global environment.
tgt: Jaaka modulasetilo, Aforika Borwa o ikaelela go maatlafatsa dikamano tsa kgwebo tsa boditšhabatšhaba ka maikaelelo a go golaganya le go oketsa seabe sa Aforika mo KPC le go tsayakarolo mo tikologong e e babalesegileng ya lefatshe.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the Restitution of Land Rights Amendment Bill 2013 and Memorandum on the Objects of the Bill, for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e rebotse go phasaladiwa ga Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa Pusetso ya Ditshwanelo tsa Lefatshe wa 2013, le Memorantamo o o ka ga Maitlhomo a Molaotlhomo, gore baagi ba tshwaele.

src: This gives effect to the President’s 2013 State of Nation Address announcement on proposed amendments to the Restitution Act.
tgt: Seno se diragatsa kitsiso ya Moporesitente ya Puo ya Maemo a Setšhaba ya 2013 malebana le dipaakanyo tse di tshitshintsweng mo go Molao wa Pusetso ya Lefatshe.

src: This relates to extending the date for lodgment of claims for restitution, to enable those parties that did not submit claims by the closing date of 31 December 1998 or who were excluded from the process, to submit.
tgt: Seno se amana le go atolosiwa ga letlha la go tsenya dkopo tsa pusetso ya lefatshe, go kgontsha ba ba sa kgonang go tsenya dkopoi ka letlha la go tswala la bo 31 Sedimonthole 1998 gongwe ba ba neng ba sa akarediwa mo tsamaisong, go dira jalo.

src: The re-opening of lodgment of claims is guided by the vision of the National Development Plan as well as the Comprehensive Rural Development Programme and other growth strategies intended to promote national reconciliation and social cohesion.
tgt: Go bulwa gape ga go tsenngwa ga dkopo go kaelwa ke ponelopele ya Leano la Tlhabololo la Bosetšhaba (NDP) mmogo le Lenaneo le le Akaretsang la Tlhabololo ya Metseselegae le maano a mangwe a kgolo a a ikaeletseng go tsweletsa poelano ya bosetšhaba le tomagano ya loago.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Electronic Communication Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e rebotse go tlhagisiwa ga Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa Tlhaeletsano ya Eleketeroniki kwa Palamenteng.

src: The amendment was necessitated by the liberalisation of the electronic communications sector and rapid technological advancements which have rendered the continued presence of some provisions in the Act redundant.
tgt: Paakanyo e tlhodilwe ke kgololesego ya lephata la tlhaeletsano ya eleketeroniki mmogo le kgolo e e bonako ya thekenoloji e e dirang gore go nna teng ga ditlamelo dingwe tsa Molao ono go se ke ga nna mosola.

src: The Amendments seeks to deal with competition promotion limitation, access to electronic communications infrastructure, communication costs as well as improving turnaround time for consultative processes.
tgt: Paakanyo e ikaelela go samagana le tekanyetso ya tsweletso ya kgaisano, phitlhelelo ya mafaratlhatlha a tlhaeletsano ya eleketeroniki, ditshenyegelo tsa eleketeroniki mmogo le go tokafatsa nako ya tsamaiso ya patloditirelo.

src: The Amendment Bill aligns the Act with broad-based black economic empowerment legislation refines licensing issues improves competition provisions removes regulatory bottlenecks and provides for matters connected to this.
tgt: Molaotlhomo wa Paakanyo o lepalepanya Molao le molao wa maatlafatso e e atolositsweng ya ikonomi ya bantsho o tokafatsa dintlha tsa dilaesense o tokafatsa ditlamelo tsa dikgaisano o tlosa dikgoreletsi tsa taolo mme o na le tlamelo ya merero e e amanang le tseno.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA) Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e rebotse go tlhagisiwa ga Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa Bothati jo bo Ikemetseng jwa Tlhaeletsano jwa Aforika Borwa (ICASA) kwa Palamenteng.

src: The Amendment Bill responds to some of the issues in the National Development Plan (NDP).The amendments of the Independent Communication Authority Act No.
tgt: Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng o tsibogela dingwe tsa dintlha tse di mo NDP.

src: 13 of 2002 (ICASA Act) are underpinned by the need for institutional improvements to strengthen the independent Authority.
tgt: Dipaakanyo tsa Molao wa Bothati jo bo Ikemetseng jwa Tlhaeletsano wa bo 13 wa 2002 (Molao wa ICASA) di tshegeditswe ke tlhokego ya ditokafatso tsa setheo go maatlafatsa Bothati jo bo Ikemetseng.

src: This will be through the provision of clarity on aspects of its powers to align the Act more closely to the requirements of the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA) and to improve its efficiency.
tgt: Seno e tla nna ka go sedifadiwa ga dintlha tsa maatla a jona go lepalepanya Molao thata le ditlhokego tsa Molao wa Tsamaiso ya Ditšhelete tsa Setšhaba le go tokafatsa bokgoni jwa bona.

src: This is with a view to improve accountability and transparency which will contribute to sound governance practices within ICASGovernment needs to play a greater role to ensure that the electronic communications sector is regulated in a manner that supports overall national goals.
tgt: Seo se dirwa go totilwe go tokafatsa maikarabelo le go direla dilo mo pepeneneng e leng se se tla tsayang karolo mo taolong e e lolameng mo teng ga ICASA.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.
tgt: Seemo sa Kabinete mo mererong e e kwa setlhoeng mo maemong a ga jaanong.

src: Cabinet calls on communities to be vigilant against the possible resurgence of criminal violence targeting foreign nationals.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo baaging go nna kelotlhoko kgatlhanong le kgonagalo ya go tsoga gape ga bosenyi jwa tirisodikgoka jo bo totileng baditšhaba.

src: Cabinet is cautious not to label this violence as xenophobia because preliminary evidence indicates that these acts may be driven primarily by criminality.
tgt: Kabinete e tila go ka re tirisodikgoka eno ke ya letlhoo la baditšhaba gonne bosupi jwa ga jaana bo supa gore ditiragalo tseno di susumediwa ke bosenyi.

src: Cabinet commended the law enforcement agencies for their swift and decisive action.
tgt: Kabinete e akgotse maphata a tiragatso ya molao ka ntlha ya dikgato tse di bonako le tse di maikaelelo.

src: Cabinet conveys its condolences to the families and friends of the young men who lost their lives as a result of inappropriate initiation ceremonies.
tgt: Kabinete e romela matshidiso kwa malapeng le kwa ditsaleng tsa makawana a a latlhegetsweng ke matshelo ka ntlha ya ditiro tse di seng maleba tsa go rupisa.

src: Cabinet endorses the call by President Jacob Zuma for swift justice and calls on traditional leaders and members of the community to be vigilant against abuse or neglect.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela boikuelo jwa Moporesitente Jacob Zuma jwa gore go diragadiwe bosiamisi ka bonako mme e ikuela mo magosing le ditokololo tsa baagi go ema kgatlhanong le tshotlakako le botlhaswa.

src: Government fully supports the traditions and cultures of our diverse society and highlights that these must be balanced with constitutional rights.
tgt: Puso e tshegetsa ditso tsa baagi ba rona ba ba farologaneng ka botlalo mme e gatelela gore di tshwanetse go lepalepana le ditshwanelo tsa molaotheo.

src: Cabinet welcomed South Africa’s participation in the recent African Union (AU) Summit, where South Africa prioritised a number of issues on the agenda of the Summit.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse seabe sa Aforika Borwa mo Samiting ya Tshwaragano ya Aforika (AU) fa gautshwane, moo Aforika Borwa e beetseng kwa pele dintlha di le mmalwa mo lenaneong la Samiti.

src: These included the Strategic Plan of the AU Commission for the period 2014-2017 and the AU Budget for 2014 the state of peace and security in Africa alternative sources of funding for the AU the post-2015 Development Agenda the meeting of the NEPAD Heads of State and Government Orientation Committee, and the African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM) Forum Summit.
tgt: Tsona di akareditse Leano la Togamaano la Khomišene ya AU mo pakeng ya 2014-2017 le Tekanyetsokabo ya AU ya 2015 seemo sa kagiso le pabalesego mo Aforika metswedi e mengwe ya tlamelo ka matlole ya AU Lenaneo la Tlhabololo la morago ga 2015 kopano ya Ditlhogo tsa Mebuso tsa Bodirisanimmogo jo Bontšhwa jwa Tlhabololo ya Aforika le Komiti ya Kitsiso ya Puso, mmogo le Samiti ya Foramo ya Thulaganyo ya Tshekatsheko ya Balekane ba Aforika.

src: Cabinet commended the Southern African Development Community (SADC) leadership for facilitating the process that led to Zimbabwe adopting a new Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e akgotse boeteledipele jwa Mokgatlho wa Tlhabololo ya Dinaga tsa Borwa jwa Aforika ka go gokaganya thulaganyo e e lebisitseng kwa goreng Zimbabwe e amogele Molaotheo o montšhwa.

src: The Zimbabwean Constitution marks a significant milestone in the successful implementation of the Global Peace Agreement.
tgt: Molaotheo wa Zimbabwe ke sesupo sa tswelelopele mo tiragatsong e e atlegang ya Tumelano ya Kagiso ya Lefatshe.

src: On the eve of Youth Month Cabinet calls on all segments of society to raise the profile of programmes to fight substance abuse.
tgt: Pele fela ga Kgwedi ya Bašwa, Kabinete e ikuela mo dikarolong tsotlhe tsa baagi go godisa manaane a a lwantshang tiriso e e botlhaswa ya diritibatsi.

src: The Youth Month theme is: “Working Together for Youth Development and a Drug Free South Africa.”Government’s decisive action to address substance abuse in Eldorado Park, Gauteng, brings the people in this area closer to the realisation of a drug-free community.
tgt: Moono wa Kgwedi ya Bašwa ke: "Re Dira Mmogo go Tlhabolola Bašwa le go bona Aforika Borwa yo o se nang Diritibatsi.

src: Cabinet notes and welcomes the progress made by the police, community leaders and other structures in Eldorado Park under the leadership of the Gauteng Provincial Government.
tgt: "Kgato ya puso ya go samagana le tiriso e e botlhaswa ya diritibatsi kwa Eldorado Park kwa Gauteng, e atametsa batho ba lefelo le gaufi le go fitlhelela go nna lefelo le le se nang diritibatsi.

src: Together they made significant progress in fighting the scourge of substance abuse.
tgt: Mmogo ba nnile le tswelelopele e e bonalang mo ntweng kgatlhanong le bosula jwa tiriso e e botlhaswa ya diritibatsi.

src: Cabinet is aware that the situation in Eldorado Park is symptomatic of issues facing many communities in the rest of the country and calls on communities throughout the country to lead the fight for a “substance-free” South Africa within their respective areas.
tgt: Kabinete e lemoga gore seemo sa kwa Eldorado Park ke sesupo sa mathata a a lebaneng bontsi jwa baagi mo nageng ka bophara mme e ikuela mo baaging go ralalala naga go etelela pele ntwa ya go fedisa diritibatsi mo Aforika Borwa mo mafelong a WEBTOKEN Kgweding ya Bašwa, tlaya re itlameng gape go lwa ntwa kgatlhanong le tiriso e e botlhaswa ya diritibatsi le botagwa mo dikarolong tsotlhe tsa naga.

src: Cabinet welcomes the incremental introduction of an African language in Grade R and Grade 1 where such languages are not yet offered.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela kitsiso e e tla okediwang ya puo ya seAforika kwa Mophatong wa R le Mophato wa 1 koo dipuo tseno di neng di sa rutiwe teng.

src: Cabinet also commends the announcement by the University of KwaZulu-Natal to make isiZulu compulsory for undergraduate students, who are not proficient in isiZulu, to register for a course to develop conversational skills.
tgt: Gape Kabinete e akgola kitsiso ya Yunibesithi ya KwaZulu-Natal ya go dira gore baithuti ba ngwaga wa ntlha, ba ba sa itseng puo ya SeZulu ba patelesege go ikwadisetsa serutwa seno gore ba oketse bokgoni jwa go tlotla.

src: Cabinet encourages all South Africans to learn an indigenous language as it promotes multilingualism and fosters nation-building.
tgt: Kabinete e rotloetsa maAforika Borwa otlhe go ithuta dipuo tsa tlholego ka ntlha ya fa seno se rotloetsa go nna dipuodintsi mme se maatlafatsa kago ya setšhaba.

src: Cabinet notes that from 1 to 3 June 2013 President Jacob Zuma will pay an official visit to Japan and attend the 5th Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD V).
tgt: Kabinete e nopotse gore go tloga ka la bo 1 go fitlha ka la bo 3 Seetebosigo 2013, Moporesitente Jacob Zuma o tla tsaya leeto la semmuso go ya Japane koo a tla tsenelang Khonferense ya Botlhano ya Boditšhabatšhaba ya Tokyo e e ka ga Tlhabololo ya Aforika (TICAD V).

src: The theme of TICAD V in Yokohama, Japan, is: “Hand in Hand with a More Dynamic Africa.”.
tgt: Moono wa TICAD V kwa Yokohama, Japan, ke: “Re tshwaragane ka diatla le Aforika e e Mafolofolo go Gaisa.”.

src: Cabinet is saddened by the passing of veteran journalist Vuyo Mbuli and offers condolences to the Mbuli family, friends and colleagues in the media industry.
tgt: Kabinete e utlwisitswe botlhoko ke loso la mankge wa mmegadikgang Vuyo Mbuli mme e romela matshidiso kwa lelapeng la ga Mbuli, kwa ditsaleng le kwa badiringmmogo ka ene mo lephateng la bobegakgang.

src: Mr Mbuli had contributed immensely to shaping the national discourse on key issues and his passion for his work had touched the hearts of South Africans.
tgt: Rre Mbuli o tsere karolo go bonala mo go rulaganyeng dikganetsano tsa bosetšhaba mo mererong ya botlhokwa mme lerato la gagwe mo tirong ya gagwe le amile dipelo tsa maAforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet expressed its deepest condolences to the citizens of Bangladesh and families and friends of over 1 000 garment factory workers who died when a building collapsed.
tgt: Kabinete e romela matshidiso kwa baaging ba kwa Bangladesh le ba malapa le ditsala tsa badiri ba le 1 000 ba feme ya diaparo ba ba tlhokafetseng fa kago e ne e gosomana.

src: Our thoughts and prayers are with the people of Bangladesh.
tgt: Re na le baagi ba Bangladesh mo megopolong le dithapelong.

src: Cabinet is deeply saddened by the loss of lives and injuries as a result of major flooding in southern China.
tgt: Kabinete e utlwisitswe botlhoko thata ke tatlhegelo ya matshelo le dikgobalo ka ntlha ya merwalela e e boitshegang kwa borweng jwa China.

src: Cabinet also expressed deep sorrow at the death of five learners from Lwandile Village in Ngqeleni, Eastern Cape, who died in a bus accident.
tgt: Gape Kabinete e tlhagisitse kutlobotlhoko ka ntlha ya dintsho tsa barutwana ba le batlhano go tswa kwa motseng wa Lwandile kwa Ngqeleni, kwa Eastern Cape, ba ba tlhokafetseng mo kotsing ya bese.

src: 30 learners were also injured during this tragic incident.
tgt: Barutwana ba le 30 ba gobetse mo kotsing eno e e masisi.

src: Government offers its condolences to the families, friends, fellow learners and educators of the victims.
tgt: Puso e romela matshidiso kwa malapeng, kwa ditsaleng le kwa barutwana ka bona le barutabana ba batswasetlhabelo.

src: It is a sad moment when South Africa loses future leaders.
tgt: Go utlwisa botlhoko fa Aforika Borwa e latlhegelwa ke baeteledipele ba isago.

src: Key Cabinet discussions and decisions.
tgt: Dipuisano le ditshweetso tse di botlhokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved that the Green Paper on Policing be published in the Government Gazette for public comments.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse gore Lokwalotshwaelo lwa Puso tebang le Sepodisi le phasaladiwe mo Lekwalodikgang la go Tlhomamisa Melao ya Puso gore baagi ba dire ditshwaelo.

src: Since the establishment of the South African Police Service (SAPS) in 1994, there have been many changes in the internal and external environment that have impacted on the Service’s understanding of and response to issues of crime and safety.
tgt: Fa e sa le go tlhamiwa Tirelo ya Sepodisi ya Aforika Borwa (SAPS) ka 1994, go nnile le diphetogo di le dintsi mo tikologong ya ka fa gare le kwa ntle, tse di amileng ka moo Tirelo e tlhaloganyang le go tsibogela merero ya bosenyi le pabalesego ka gona.

src: Post-1994, government was faced with addressing the twin objectives of creating a developmental state while also transforming the police into an institution of governance.
tgt: Morago ga 1994, puso e ne e lebanwe ke go samagana le maitlhomo a le mabedi a go tlhama mmuso o o tlhabologang mme gape e ntse e fetola sepodisi go nna setheo sa taolo.

src: This Green Paper responds to the challenges identified following an assessment of the relevance of the 1996 Crime Prevention Strategy (NCPS) and the 1998 White paper on Safety and Security.
tgt: Lokwalotshwaelo lwa Puso leno le tsibogela dikgwetlho tse di supilweng go latela tshekatsheko ya bomaleba jwa Togamaano ya Thibelo ya Bosenyi ya Bosetšhaba ya 1996 le Lokwalotemoso lwa puso lwa 1998 le le ka ga Pabalesego le Tshireletsego.

src: Embedded in these policies was the notion of addressing safety and security in a holistic manner through the development and implementation of integrated cross-sectoral programmes.
tgt: Mo teng ga dipholisi tseno go ne go na le ntlha ya go samagana le pabalesego le tshireletsego ka tsela e e akaretsang tlhabololo le go tsenngwa tirisong ga manaane a a kopaneng a a kgabaganyang maphata.

src: Together they sought to put in place a comprehensive framework for dealing with broader issues of safety and security until 2004.The Green Paper deals with “Confronting Crime in a Democratic South Africa, Policing in South Africa, Mainstreaming Police Profssionalism and Institutional Arrangements”.
tgt: Ka bobedi, di ne di batla go tlhoma letlhomeso le le akaretsang la go samagana le merero ya pabalesego le tshireletsego ka bophara go fitlha ka 2004.Lokwalotshwaelo lwa Puso le bua ka "Go Tota Bosenyi mo go Aforika Borwa wa Temokerasi, Sepodisi mo Aforika Borwa, Go Tiisa Boporofešenale jwa Sepodisi gammogo le Dithulaganyo tsa Setheo."

src: This aims to ultimately position the SAPS to respond to a constantly evolving criminal landscape while simultaneously meeting the needs of a developmental state.
tgt: Maikaelelo a seno ke go baya SAPS mo maemong a go kgona go tsibogela bosenyi jo bo nnang bo fetoga mme e ntse gape e fitlhelela ditlhokego tsa Mmuso o o tlhabologang.

src: Cabinet approved the National Plan of Action for Children 2012-2017 as the comprehensive plan to give guidance and direction to government departments, civil society and other partners in the children’s sector towards the realisation of children’s rights.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetsa Leano la Bosetšhaba la Dikgato Tebang le Bana la 2012-2017 jaaka leano le le akaretsang le e tla nnang kaedi le mosupatsela wa mafapha a puso, baagi le balekane ba bangwe mo lephateng la bana go lebisa kwa go fitlheleleng ditshwanelo tsa bana.

src: The plan embraces the Constitution, international and regional treaties, the emerging legislation on children in South Africa, Millennium Development Goals and the National Development Plan Vision 2030.The plan has five main themes: child survival (e. g. reduction of child mortality) child development (e. g. early childhood development services) child protection (e. g. protection from violence and sexual abuse) standard of living of children (e. g. conditions on accommodation for children) and child participation (e. g. children taking responsibility while enjoying their rights).This National Plan of Action for Children 2012-2017 will be further unpacked during a separate media briefing.
tgt: Leano le akaretsa Molaotheo, ditumelano tsa boditšhabatšhaba le tsa kgaolo, molao o o tlhagelelang wa bana mo Aforika Borwa, Diphitlhelelo tsa Tlhabololo tsa Ngwagakete gammogo le Ponelopele ya Leano la Tlhabololo la Bosetšhaba (NDP) ya 2030.Leano le na le meono e megolo e le metlhano: go tshela ga bana (sekao.

src: The Charter is aligned to the New Growth Path, the National Development Plan, the White Paper on Arts, Culture and Heritage and the Mzansi Golden Economy Strategy.
tgt: Tlhomamiso ya Tumelano ke puso ke go tsibogela Kgoeletso ya tsosoloso ya Setso le Ditumelo tse di Aroganwang ya Kopano ya Tlwaelo ya bo 16 ya Ditlhogo tsa Dinaga le Mebuso ya AU e e neng e tshwaretswe kwa Equatorial Guinea ka Ferikgong 2011, le go tlhomiwa ga Letsholo la AU la Tumelano ya Tsosoloso ya Setso sa Aforika le le neng le tshwerwe go ya kwa bokhutlong jwa 2011 mo Aforika Borwa.

src: The Minster of Arts and Culture will host a media briefing in this regard.
tgt: Tlhomamiso ya Tumelano e tokafatsa tshireletso ya ditumelo tsa setso tsa seAforika le ngwaoboswa ya setso mme e tsweletsa mowa wa BoAforika.

src: Cabinet noted the hosting of the first Science, Technology and Innovation Summit from 20 to 21 July 2013.The planned dialogue during the Summit provides a platform to explore ways to enhance coordination between government and the private sector.
tgt: Tumelano e tsweletsa kopano ya setso, botsweretshi, ditumelo tsa setso, puo, ngwaoboswa mmogo le diintaseteri tsa setso le boitlhamedi jaaka mooko wa tlhabololo ya leruri.

src: The Summit will enable participants to explore ways in which science, technology and innovation (STI) can play a significant role in our journey towards a knowledge-based economy and realisation of Vision Bills.
tgt: Seno se ka nna le bokgoni jwa go tsayakarolo mo kgolong ya ikonomi le mo go nneng seoposengwe.

src: Cabinet approved the proposed amendments to the Draft Public Administration Management (PAM) Bill which will now be published for public comment.
tgt: Tumelano e lepalepane le Tsela e Ntšhwa ya Kgolo, NDP, Lokwalotemoso lwa Puso lwa Botsweretshi, Setso le Ngwaoboswa mmogo le Togamaano ya Mzansi ya Ikonomi ya Gauta.

src: Cabinet approved the Public Service Commission Amendment Bill for public comment and the introduction of the Amendment Bill in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse dipaakanyo tse di tshitshintsweng mo Molaotlhomong wa Botsamaisi jwa Tsamaiso ya Setšhaba (PAM) o jaanong o tla phasaladiwang gore baagi ba tshwaele mo go ona.

src: The purpose of the Amendment Bill is to align the Public Service Commission Act of 1997 with the Constitution.
tgt: Molaotlhomo o ikaelela go tlhama letlhomeso le le tshwanang la molao la tsamaiso ya badiri le merero mengwe ya ditheo le taolo mo ditsamaisong tsa bosetšhaba, porofense le makgotlatoropo.

src: It further seeks to empower the Public Service Commission to give directions relating to the principles that govern public administration.
tgt: Maikaelelo a seno ke go tokafatsa tlamelo ya ditirelo ka thulaganyo e e tshwanang ya tsamaiso ya setšhaba, tiriso e e tokafaetseng ya badiri mmogo le go tlhamela baagi mafelo a le mangwe fela a ditirelo tsotlhe tsa puso.

src: This is in line with the strengthened role envisaged by the National Development Plan for the Commission.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa Khomišene ya Tirelo ya Setšhaba gore baagi ba tshwaele mmogo le go itsisewe ga Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng kwa Palamenteng.

src: Cabinet approved that the South African Weather Service Amendment Bill 2013 be published for public comment.
tgt: Maitlhomo a Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng ke go lepalepanya Molao wa Khomišene ya Tirelo ya Setšhaba wa 1997 le Molaotheo.

src: This Amendment Bill seeks to amend the South African Weather Services Act, 2001 (Act No.
tgt: Seno se ikamanya le seabe se se maatlafaditsweng se se solofetsweng mo Khomišeneng ke NDKabinete e amogetse gore Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa Tirelo ya Maemo A Bosa ya Aforika Borwa wa 2013 o phasaladiwe gore setšhaba se tshwaele.

src: 08 of 2001) which provides for the establishment, objectives, powers and functions of the South African Weather WEBTOKEN the main the amendments will provide the South African Weather Service with a legal mandate to implement the ambient air quality information management function, and to act as a custodian of the South African Air Quality information System.
tgt: Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng o ikaelela go baakanya Molao wa Tirelo ya Maemo a Bosa ya Aforika Borwa wa 2001, (Molao wa bo 08 wa 2001) o o nang le ditlamelo tsa go tlhamiwa, maikaelelo, maatla le ditiro tsa Tirelo ya Maemo a Bosa ya Aforika Borwa.

src: This contributes towards protecting and enhancing our environmental assets and natural resources.
tgt: Maitlhomomagolo ke dipaakanyo tse di tla tlamelang Tirelo ya Maemo a Bosa ya Aforika Borwa ka thomo ya semolao go diragatsa tiro ya tsamaiso ya tshedimosetso ya boleng jwa mowa, mmogo le go dira jaaka motlhokomedi wa Thulaganyo ya Tshedimosetso ya Boleng jwa Mowa ya Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet approved that the Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Draft Amendment Bill, 2012 be submitted to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse gore Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa Tlhabololo ya Ditlamelo tsa Diminerale le Peteroliamo wa 2012 o tlhagisiwe kwa Palamenteng.

src: The Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Draft Amendment Bill 2012 (Draft Bill) seeks to amend the Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Act, 2002 (Act No.
tgt: Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa Tlhabololo ya Ditlamelo tsa Diminerale le Peteroliamo wa 2012 (Molaotlhomo) o ikaelela go baakanya Molao wa Tlhabololo ya Ditlamelo tsa Diminerale le Peteroliamo wa 2002 (Molao wa bo 28 wa 2002) jaaka o baakantswe ke Molao o o Baakantsweng wa Tlhabololo ya Ditlamelo tsa Diminerale le Peteroliamo wa 2008 (Molao wa bo 49 wa 2008).Maikaelelo a ntlha a Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng, gareng ga tse dingwe, ke go tokafatsa tlamelo ya go fetolwa ga diminerale gore go tswelediwe madirelo le go tshwaela mo maitlhomomg a setšhaba a go tlhamiwa ga ditiro le kgolo ya ikonomi jaaka a lebeletswe mo NDGo tla nna le kopano e e farologaneng ya bobegakgang malebana le seno.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment Cabinet wishes President Nelson Mandela a speedy recovery and reassures the nation that he is receiving the best medical care.
tgt: Kabinete e eleletsa Moporesitente wa maloba Nelson Mandela go sidilega ka bonako mme e netefaletsa setšhaba gore o amogela tlhokomelo e e gaisang ya kalafi.

src: Cabinet is pleased that he is responding well to treatment and reiterates the request for the media and the public to respect the privacy of the former President and his family during this period.
tgt: Kabinete e lebogela gore o tsibogela kalafi sentle mme e boeletsa boikuelo jwa gore bobegakgang le setšhaba ba tlotle sebaka sa Moporesitente wa maloba le balelapa la gagwe mo pakeng eno.

src: Cabinet commends the work of the Justice, Crime, Prevention and Security Cluster’s Anti-Corruption Task Team (ACTT) which was established by President Jacob Zuma in 2010.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola tiro ya Setlhopha sa Tiro se se Kgatlhanong le Bobodu sa Lephata la Bosiamisi, Thibelo ya Bosenyi le Tshireletsego (ACTT) se se tlhamilweng ke Moporesitente Jacob Zuma ka 2010.

src: For the first time in the history of our democracy, criminals who had abused public trust and resources were made known and held accountable for their actions publicly.
tgt: La ntlha mo hisetoring ya temokerasi ya rona, basenyi ba ba dirisitseng botlhaswa ditlamelo tsa setšhaba le boikanyego, ba senotswe mme ba rwesiwa maikarabelo a ditiro tsa bona mo phatlhalatseng.

src: South Africa’s zero tolerance to corruption takes us closer to our vision for 2030 where South African society is characterised by high ethical standards and integrity.
tgt: Go se batle go itshokela bobodu ga Aforika Borwa go re atametsa gaufi le ponelopele ya rona ya 2030, moo setšhaba sa Aforika Borwa se tla bong se rena maitsholo a maemo a a kwa godimo le boikanyego.

src: This aggressive stance aims to deter people in the private and public sectors from engaging in corrupt and criminal activities and is driven by our commitment to ensure that all citizens are and feel safe.
tgt: Seemo seno sa tšhakgalo se ikaelela go thibela batho ba ba mo maphateng a poraefete le a setšhaba go dira ditiro tsa bobodu le bosenyi mme se tsamaisiwa ke maitlamo a rona a go netefatsa gore baagi botlhe ba gololesegile mme ba ikutlwa ba babalesegile.

src: Cabinet condemns in the strongest terms the recent acts of racism in some parts of our country.
tgt: Kabinete e kgala ka mafoko a a bogale ditiragalo tsa sešweng tsa bosemorafe mo dikarolong dingwe tsa naga ya rona.

src: There is no room for racism in our country and democracy, let alone in our schools, where the values of our Constitution ought to be promoted and defended.
tgt: Bosemorafe ga bo na sebaka mo nageng le mo temokerasing ya rona, bogolo segolo kwa dikolong tsa rona koo go tshwanetseng ga tswelediwa le go sireletsa dintlhatheo tsa Molaotheo wa rona gone.

src: Cabinet commends the Department of Basic Education for its quick action in dealing with racism in schools and encourages all parents, pupils, and teachers to report racism and abuse at schools.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola Lefapha la Thuto ya Motheo ka tsibogo ya lona e e bonako malebana le go samagana le bosemorafe kwa dikolong mme e rotloetsa batsadi, barutwana, le barutabana go bega bosemorafe le tshotlakako kwa dikolong.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to work together with government to get deal with racism whenever it occurs in our society.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo maAforika Borweng otlhe go dira mmogo le puso go lwantsha bosemorafe nako nngwe le nngwe fa bo tlhagelela mo setšhabeng sa rona.

src: Cabinet welcomes the visit to the Republic of South Africa by the President of the United States of America (US), Barack Obama which is part of a three-nation visit to Senegal, Tanzania and South Africa between 26 June and 3 July 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela ketelo ya mo Rephaboliking ya Aforika Borwa ke Moporesitente wa Amerika, Barack Obama, jaaka karolo ya ketelo ya dinaga di le tharo tsa Senegal, Tanzania le Aforika Borwa magareng ga la bo 26 Seetebosigo le la bo 3 Phukwi 2013.

src: Our strategic political dialogue with the United States continues to positively impact our bilateral relations.
tgt: Dipuisano tsa rona tsa togamaano tsa sepolotiki le Amerika di tswelela go nna le ditlamorago tse di namatshang mo botsalanong jwa rona jwa sebedi.

src: The US remains an important trade, investment, tourism and technology partner.
tgt: Amerika e sa ntse e le molekane wa botlhokwa wa kgwebisano, dipeeletso, bojanala le thekenoloji.

src: Cabinet commended the landmark meeting on the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme (KPCS) held between 4 and 7 June 2013 in Kimberley.
tgt: Kabinete e akgotse kopano ya botlhokwa e e ka ga Sekema sa Makwalonetefaletso a go Rafša sa Kimberley (KPCS), e e neng e tshwerwe magareng ga la bo 4 le la bo 7 Seetebosigo 2013 kwa Kimberley.

src: The Summit discussed amongst other things ways of strengthening the effectiveness of the rough diamond certification scheme.
tgt: Gareng ga tse dingwe, Samiti e buisanetse ditsela tsa go maatlafatsa bokgoni jwa sekema sa makwalonetefaletso a taemane e e sa rafšwang.

src: This is to ensure that diamond trade does not finance violence by rebel movements and their allies that seek to undermine legitimate governments.
tgt: Seno ke go netefatsa gore kgwebo ya ditaemane ga e tlamele matlole a tirisodikgoka ya mekgatlho ya marabele le ditsala tsa bona tse di ikaeletseng go nyatsa dipuso tse di mo molaong.

src: Recommendations from this meeting will be considered at the plenary meeting of the KPCS to be held later this year.
tgt: Dikatlenigiso tsa kopano eno di tla lebelelwa kwa kopanong ya KPCS e e tla tshwarwang moragonyana monongwaga.

src: Cabinet noted that the commemoration of Youth Day which in 2013 marks the 37th anniversary of June 16 Soweto Uprising will be celebrated under the theme “Working together for youth development and a drug free South Africa”.
tgt: Kabinete e nopotse gore segopotso sa Letsatsi la Bašwa se e leng gore mo ngwageng wa 2013 e tla bo e le segopotso sa bo 37 sa Dikhuduego tsa kwa Soweto tsa Seetebosigo a le 16, se tla bo se ketekwa ka moono wa "Re dira mmogo go tlhabolola bašwa le go fitlhelela Aforika Borwa yo o senang diritibatsi."

src: Cabinet acknowledged the sacrifices made by the class of 1976 in turning the history of the country and setting South Africa firmly on the road to democracy.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile go intsha setlhabelo ga barutwana ba 1976 ka go fetola hisetori ya naga le go tlhoma Aforika Borwa mo tseleng ya temokerasi.

src: Cabinet reiterated that, while the youth of 1976 fought for freedom and the creation of a democratic state, today’s youth activism is directed towards successfully tackling the challenges of combating poverty, unemployment, HIV and AIDS, personal development and drug abuse.
tgt: Kabinete e boeleditse gore, fa bašwa ba 1976 ba ne ba lwela kgololesego le go tlhamiwa ga mmuso wa temokerasi, kgaratlho ya bašwa gompieno e lebisitse kwa go atlegeng go samagana le dikgwetlho tsa go lwantsha lehuma, botlhokatiro, HIV le AIDS, go itlhabolola, le tiriso e e botlhaswa ya diritibatsi.

src: Cabinet encourages all South Africans and organisations to work together to improve the lives of young people and fight to remove the drug dealers within our communities.
tgt: Kabinete e rotloetsa maAforika Borwa otlhe le ditheo go dira mmogo go tokafatsa matshelo a bašwa le go lwela go tlosa ba ba gwebang ka diritibatsi mo ditšhabeng tsa rona.

src: The national Youth Day commemoration will take place on Sunday, 16 June 2013 in Newcastle, KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Segopotso sa bosetšhaba sa Letsatsi la Bašwa se tla ketekwa ka Sontaga, Seetebosigo 16, 2013 kwa Newcastle, KwaZulu-Natal.

src: Cabinet congratulates the Congress of South African Students (Cosas) on its 34th anniversary, which has its roots in the Soweto 1976 struggle for free, quality and relevant education.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola Khonkerese ya Baithuti ba Aforika Borwa (Cosas) ka segopotso sa bona sa bo 34, se modi wa sona e leng kgaratlho ya Soweto ya 1976 ya thuto e e sa duelelweng, ya boleng le e e maleba.

src: The country joins Cosas in celebrating its remarkable achievements and in advancing quality education for all.
tgt: Naga e ikgolaganya le Cosas fa e keteka diphitlhelelo tsa yona tse di namatshang tsa go fitlhelela thuto ya boleng go botlhe.

src: Cabinet also commends the leadership of Cosas for taking the initiative to rally young people against drug abuse.
tgt: Gape Kabinete e akgola boeteledipele jwa Cosas ka ntlha ya go tsaya kgato ya go rotloetsa bašwa go ema kgatlhanong le tiriso e e botlhaswa ya diritibatsi.

src: Cabinet condemns the acts of public dumping of human waste in the Western Cape by the protestors against portable bucket toilets.
tgt: Kabinete e kgala dikgato tsa go tshololela mantle a batho kwa Kapa Bophirima ke badiraditshupetso ba ba leng kgatlhanong le matlwanaboithusetso a a sutisiwang.

src: While, Government respects citizens’ right to protest, this particular form of protest is undignified and poses a serious health risk to communities and to the protesters themselves.
tgt: Le fa Puso e tlotla ditshwanelo tsa baagi go dira ditshupetso, mofuta ono wa go dira ditshupetso ga o na seriti mme o baya baagi le bona bangongoregi, mo matshosetsing a a masisi a boitekanelo.

src: Cabinet calls on citizens to raise their grievances constructively and to treat public institutions with utmost respect irrespective of their grievances.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo baaging botlhe go tlhagisa dingongorego tsa bona ka tsela e e agang le go tlotla ditheo tsa setšhaba go sa kgathalesege dingongorego tsa bona.

src: Cabinet further called on authorities to speedily address issues in a manner that is in keeping with our Constitution.
tgt: Gape kabinete e ikuela mo bothating go tsibogela dintlha ka bonako le ka tsela e e lepalepaneng le Molaotheo wa rona.

src: Government, under the leadership of Deputy President Kgalema Motlanthe, met with religious leaders representing the South Africa Council of Churches and the South African Catholic Bishops' Conference (SACBC) to discuss their concerns that the Gauteng Freeway Improvement Project (GFIP) will impact on the poor and that government was insensitive to the needs of the poor.
tgt: Puso, ka fa tlase ga boeteledipele jwa Motlatsamoporesitente Kgalema Motlanthe, e kopane le baeteledipele ba sedumedi ba ba emetseng Lekgotla la Dikereke la Aforika Borwa mmogo le Khonferense ya Babišopo ba Katoliki ba Aforika Borwa go buisana nabo malebana le matshwenyego a bona a gore Porojeke ya Tokafatso ya Ditselafefo tsa Gauteng e tla ama bahumanegi le gore puso e ikgatholositse ditlhokego tsa bahumanegi.

src: Cabinet re-iterates that government has exempted registered public transport (which is largely used by the poor) from the toll tariffs on the Gauteng toll roads.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa gape gore puso e golotse dipalangwa tse di kwadisitsweng tsa botlhe (tse di dirisiwang bogolo ke bahumanegi) mo dituelong tsa ditselakgethiso mo ditselakgethisong tsa Gauteng.

src: Also, to address the concerns of the other motorist, government has reduced the tariffs and introduced new capped amounts for all categories of vehicles.
tgt: Gape, go samagana le matshwenyego a boradijanaga ba bangwe, puso e fokoditse dituelo mme ya itsise selekano se sentšhwa sa dikarolo tsotlhe tsa dijanaga.

src: Cabinet encourages motorists in Gauteng to register for e-tags and to view this project as part of the country's drive to build public infrastructure.
tgt: Kabinete e rotloetsa boradijanaga ba Gauteng go ikwadisetsa di-e-tag le go tsaya porojeke eno jaaka karolo ya letsholo la naga la go aga mafaratlhatlha a bosetšhaba.

src: Cabinet congratulates Bafana Bafana and Banyana Banyana Soccer Teams and the Proteas Cricket Team on their recent wins in football and cricket.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola Ditlhopha tsa Kgwele ya Dinao tsa Bafana Bafana le Banyana Banyana gammogo le Setlhopha sa Khirikete sa Proteas ka diphenyo tsa tsona tsa fa gautshwane mo kgweleng ya dinao le khirikete.

src: Cabinet congratulates the national teams on their hard-fought victories over the past week and encourages all South Africans to support our national teams.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola ditlhopha tsa bosetšhaba ka diphenyo tsa tsona tse di neng di se bonolo mo bekeng e e fetileng mme e rotloetsa maAforika Borwa otlhe go tshegetsa ditlhopha tsa rona tsa bosetšhaba.

src: Cabinet welcomed the launch of Power FM, a new talk-radio station, as a new player in the industry.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse go tlhomiwa ga Power FM, seteišene se sentšhwa sa radio ya dipuisano, jaaka motshameki yo montšhwa mo indasetering.

src: Cabinet noted that the station will deal with politics, social issues and sport in the main and joins a list of radio platforms that can be used to inform South Africans.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile gore seteišene se tla samagana thata le dipolotiki, merero ya loago le metshameko mme se tsena mo lenaaneng la didiriswa tsa radio tse di ka dirisediwang go sedimosetsa maAforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet congratulates the Department of Health Director General, Dr Malebona Precious Matsoso, on her appointment as a member and one of the Vice chairpersons of the World Health Assembly Executive Board for a period of 3 years.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola Mokaedikakaretso wa Lefapha la Boitekanelo, Ngaka Malebona Precious Matsoso, ka go thapiwa ga gagwe jaaka tokololo le mongwe wa Bathusabadulasetilo ba Botokhuduthamaga ya Kokoano ya Boitekanelo ya Lefatshe sebaka sa dingwaga di le Dipuisano le ditshwetso tse di botlhokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Key Cabinet discussions and decisions Cabinet noted that the Financial Intelligence Centre of South Africa will host the 2013 Annual Plenary and General Working Group Meetings of the Egmont Group of financial intelligence units.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile gore Tikwatikwe ya Matlhale a Ditšhelete ya Aforika Borwa e tla amogela Dikopano tsa 2013 tsa Togomaano ya Ngwaga le Ngwaga le tsa Setlhophatiro Kakaretso tsa Setlhopha sa Egmont sa diyuniti tsa matlhale a ditšhelete.

src: The Egmont Group is an organisation of financial intelligence units from 131 countries.
tgt: Setlhopha sa Egmont ke mokgatlho wa diyuniti tsa matlhale a ditšhelete go tswa dinageng di le 131.

src: They meet regularly to enable international cooperation to identify the proceeds of crime, combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism with the objective of defending the integrity of the financial system.
tgt: Se kopana gangwe le gape go kgontsha tirisanommogo ya boditšhabatšhaba go supa dipoelo tsa bosenyi, go lwantsha go gweba go go seng mo molaong ka madi mmogo le go tlamela borukhutlhi ka matlole ka maitlhomo a go femela boikanyego jwa thulaganyo ya ditšhelete.

src: Cabinet noted the election of South Africa to serve on the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) for the period 2013 - 2015.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile go tlhophiwa ga Aforika Borwa go dira mo Lekgotleng la Ikonomi le Loago la Ditšhabakopano (ECOSOC) mo pakeng ya 2013 - 2015.

src: This presents an opportunity to strategically position South Africa’s leadership on development issues and reinforce the country’s role as a consistent and effective player in multilateralism.
tgt: Seno se naya tšhono ya go baya ketapele ya Aforika Borwa ka tsela ya togamaano mo mererong ya tlhabololo le go maatlafatsa seabe sa naga jaaka motsayakarolo yo o tsepameng le yo o mosola mo mererong ya bontsi.

src: South Africa will also ensure that ECOSOC is further strengthened and reformed to better meet evolving global challenges and the needs of developing countries.
tgt: Gape Aforika Borwa e tla netefatsa gore ECOSOC e maatlafadiwa gape le go fetolwa go fitlhelela botoka dikgwetlho tse di golang tsa lefatshe le ditlhokego tsa dinaga tse di tlhabologang.

src: Cabinet noted the report on South Africa’s Non-Permanent membership of the United Nations Security Council from 1 January 2011 to 31 December 2012.The report describes South Africa’s influence in the global governance system in the maintenance of international peace and security.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile pegelo e e ka ga botokololo jo E seng jwa Leruri jwa Aforika Borwa kwa Lekgotleng la Tshireletso la Ditšhabakopano (UNSC) go tloga ka la bo 1 Ferikgong go fitlha ka la bo 31 Sedimonthole 2012.Pegelo e tlhalosa tshusumetso ya Aforika Borwa mo thulaganyong ya tsamaiso ya lefatshe mo go tsholeng kagiso le tshireletso ya boditšhabatšhaba.

src: In line with its values and national interests, South Africa in the UNSC prioritised conflict resolution and peace and stability on the African Continent.
tgt: Go lepalepana le dintlhatheo le dikgatlhego tsa yona tsa bosetšhaba, Aforika Borwa le UNSC di beile tharabololo ya dikgotlhang le kagiso le tsepamo mo Kontinenteng ya Aforika jaaka ditlapele.

src: Membership of the UNSC also provided South Africa with an opportunity to strengthen relations with key developing country partners - Brazil, India, Nigeria and China - who shared Council membership with South Africa.
tgt: Botokololo jwa UNSC gape bo tlametse Aforika Borwa ka tšhono ya go maatlafatsa botsalano le balekane ba botlhokwa ba dinaga tse di tlhabologang - Brazil, India, Nigeria le China - ba ba neng ba arogana botokololo jwa Lekgotla le Aforika Borwa.

src: Bills Cabinet approved that the Disaster Management Amendment Bill be published for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse gore Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa Tsamaiso ya Matlhotlhapelo o phasaladiwe gore setšhaba se tshwaele.

src: This Bill aims to address the challenges which are being experienced across the spheres of government after commencement of the Disaster Management Act 2002.
tgt: Maikaelelo a Molaotlhomo ke go samagana le dikgwetlho tse di itemogelwang go ralala magato a puso morago ga go simolola ga Molao wa Tsamaiso ya Matlhotlhapelo wa 2002.

src: The Amendment will re-affirm the function of district municipalities regarding the responsibility to establish capacity for the development and coordination of a disaster management plan.
tgt: Paakanyo e tla tlhomamisa gape tiro ya makgotlatoropo a kgaolo malebana le maikarabelo a go tlhama bokgoni jwa go tlhama le go gokaganya leano la tsamaiso ya matlhotlhapelo.

src: This includes the implementation of a disaster management function for the municipal area.
tgt: Seno se akaretsa go tsenngwa tirisong ga tiro ya tsamaiso ya matlhotlhapelo mo karolong ya lekgotlatoropo.

src: The Disaster Management Act 2002 has a fourfold focus: It establishes an elaborate institutional framework for disaster management it entrenches a detailed policy development and strategic planning framework for disaster management.
tgt: Molao wa Tsamaiso ya Matlhotlhapelo wa 2002 o na le tebo ya maphata a le mane: O tlhama letlhomeso le le bonalang la setheo sa tsamaiso ya matlhotlhapelo o akaretsa tlhabololo ya pholisi ka botlalo gammogo le letlhomeso la togamaano ya tsamaiso ya matlhotlhapelo.

src: The bill further provides for the classification and declaration of disaster and it deals provisionally with the funding of post-disaster recovery and rehabilitation.
tgt: Gape molaotlhomo o na le tlamelo ya karoganyo le kgoeletso ya matlhotlhapelo mme o samagana nakwana le matlole a pusetso le tsosoloso ya morago ga matlhotlhapelo.

src: It provides for disaster management volunteers and a few other ancillary matters.
tgt: O na le tlamelo ya baithaopi ba tsamaiso ya matlhotlhapelo gammogo le merero e mengwe ya tlaleletso.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Local Government Municipal property Rates Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e rebotse go tlhagisiwa ga Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa Pusoselegae wa Kgethiso ya matlo a Makgotlatoropo kwa Palamenteng.

src: The Local Government: Municipal Property rates Act became effective on 2 July 2005.
tgt: Pusoselegae: Molao wa kgethiso ya matlo a Makgotlatoropo o simolotse go dira ka la bo 2 Phukwi 2005.

src: It was amended twice in 2008 and 2009.
tgt: O baakantswe gabedi ka 2008 le 2009.

src: The amendments seek to remove ambiguity and provide greater legal certainty.
tgt: Paakanyo e ikaelela go tlosa ketsaetsego le go tlamela ka tlhaloso e kgolwane ya semolao.

src: The amendment will allow for transparency in the setting of rates for different property categories, thus enhancing property owners understanding of rating.
tgt: Paakanyo e tla dira gore go bewa ga lekgetho la dikarolo tse di farologaneng tsa matlo go direlwe mo pepeneneng, mme ka go rialo go tokafatsa gore beng ba matlo ba tlhaloganye lekgetho.

src: The amendment will exclude certain public service infrastructure (PSI) such as roads, railways, airports aprons and runways, dams and breakwater from being rated.
tgt: Paakanyo e ka se ke ya akaretsa mafaratlhatlha mangwe a tirelosetšhaba a tshwana le ditsela, diporo, mafelo a difofane di tsoramang mo go one le ao di tlhatlhogang mo go one, matamo le magora a maemelakepe mo kgethisong.

src: These are publicly controlled and will not disadvantage private sectors.
tgt: Tseno di laolwa ke setšhaba mme di ka seke tsa lomeletsa lephata la poraefete.

src: This would enhance economic activity across municipal boundaries.
tgt: Seno se tla tokafatsa motsamao wa ikonomi go ralala melelwane ya makgotlatoropo.

src: It would also contribute to the developmental role of SOEs by reducing their fixed costs.
tgt: Gape se tla tshwaela mo seabeng sa tlhabololo sa Dikgwebo tse di Tsamaisiwang ke Puso ka go fokotsa ditshenyegelo tse di tsepameng.

src: Cabinet approved a battery of Merchant Shipping Legislation for tabling in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse maatla a Molao wa Tsamaiso ka Dikepe Dilwana tse di Rekisiwang go tlhagisiwa mo Palamenteng.

src: These Bills form part of a package of measures designed to give effect to South Africa’s obligations under the International Maritime Organisation Protocol of 1992.
tgt: Melaotlhomo eno ke karolo ya setlhopha sa dikgato tse di rulaganyeditsweng go diragatsa maikarabelo a Aforika Borwa ka fa tlase ga Thulaganyo ya Mekgatlho ya Mawatle ya Boditšhabatšhaba ya 1992.1 Maitlhomo a Molaotlhomo wa Tsamaiso ka Dikepe Dilwana tse di Rekisiwang (Tumelano ya Maikarabelo a Setšhaba) ke go: tlhomamisa Thulaganyo ya Mekgatlho ya Mawatle ya Boditšhabatšhaba ya 1992 le go fetisa Tumelano ya 1969 e e baakantsweng ya Boditšhabatšhaba e e ka ga Maikarabelo a Setšhaba malebana le Tshenyo ya Kgotlhelego ya Oli, go nna molao.

src: .1 The purpose of the Merchant Shipping (Civil Liability Convention) Bill is to: enact International Maritime Organisation Protocol, 1992 and to pass into law the amended International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage, 1969.
tgt: Tumelano ya Maikarabelo a Setšhaba e tlhama le go laola maikarabelo a mong yo o kwadisitsweng wa sekepe.2 Maikaelelo a Molaotlhomo wa Tsamaiso ka Dikepe Dilwana tse di Rekisiwang (Letlole la Boditšhabatšhaba la Tuelo ya go Kgotlhelwa ke Oli) ke go: tsenya tirisong Thulaganyo ya 1992 mo Sebokeng sa Boditšhabatšhaba ka ga Go Tlhamiwa ga Letlole la Boditšhabatšhaba la Tuelo ya Ditshenyegelo tsa go Kgotlhelwa ke Oli la 1971 (Seboka sa Letlole).Seboka sa Letlole se tlhama Letlole la Boditšhabatšhaba, le le bidiwang Letlole la Boditšhabatšhaba la Tuelo ya Tshenyegelo ka go Kgotlhelwa ke Oli (IOPC).

src: The Civil Liability Convention establishes and regulates the liability of the registered ship owner.
tgt: Maitlhomo a Letlole ke go duela batswasetlhabelo ba tshenyegelo ka kgotlhelego (go kaegilwe ka bokao jwa Tumelano ya Maikarabelo a Setšhaba) moo ba sa kgonang go bona tuelo, gongwe tuelo ka botlalo, ka fa tlase ga ditlamelo tsa Tumelano ya Maikarabelo a Setšhaba.

src: .2 The aim of the Merchant Shipping (International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund) Bill is to: implement the 1992 Protocol to the International Convention on the Establishment of an International Fund for Compensation for Oil Pollution Damage, 1971 (the Fund Convention).
tgt: Molaotlhomo wa Ditumelano tsa Maikarabelo a Setšhaba le Letlole o samagana le dintlha tsa maikarabelo le tuelo ya ditshenyegelo le tshenyo e e bakilweng ke kgotlhelego e e bakilweng ke go sutlha kgotsa go tswena go go tswelelang ga oli go tswa mo ditankeng.3 Molaotlhomo wa Tsamaiso ka Dikepe Dilwana tse di Rekisiwang (Letlole la Boditšhabatšhaba la Tuelo ya go Kgotlhelwa ke Oli) le Kabelo mmogo le Molaotlhomo wa Tsamaiso ka Dikepe Dilwana tse di Rekisiwang (Letlole la Boditšhabatšhaba la Tuelo ya go Kgotlhelwa ke Oli) wa Botsamaisi e dira tlamelo ya go tsenngwa tirisong ga Thulaganyo ya Boditšhabatšhaba ya Mokgatlho wa Mawatle wa 1992 go baakanya Tumelano ya Boditšhabatšhaba e e ka ga go Tlhamiwa ga Letlole la Boditšhabatšhaba la Tshenyegelo ya Kgotlhelego ka Oli, ke Aforika Borwa.

src: The Fund Convention establishes an international Fund, called the International Oil Pollution Compensation (IOPC) Fund.
tgt: Molaotlhomo wa Tsamaiso o tla tlamela ka taolo e e tlhokegang ya molao go kgontsha ba Ditirelo tsa Letseno la Aforika Borwa go tsamaisa kokoanyo ya tefiso ya Kabelo ya Letlole la Boditšhabatšhaba la Tuelo ya Kgotlhelego ka Oli.

src: The purpose of the Fund is to pay compensation to victims of pollution damage (within the meaning of the Civil Liability Convention) where they have been unable to obtain compensation, or compensation in full, under the provisions of the Civil Liability Convention.
tgt: Molaotlhomo wa Kabelo ke Molaotlhomo wa tšhelete o o dirang tlamelo ya go tsenya tirisong le go kokoanya dikabelo tse di tshwanetse go duelwa Letlole.

src: Ms Muditambi Raveled.
tgt: Rre Goliath Munro.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment Cabinet joins the nation and the international community in praying for the father of the nation, former President Nelson Mandela.
tgt: Kabinete e ikgolaganya le setšhaba le baagi ba boditšhabatšhaba go rapelela rrasetšhaba, e leng Moporesitente wa maloba Nelson Mandela.

src: At this difficult time, let us all show love and compassion and make Madiba proud.
tgt: Mo nakong eno e e masisi, tla re bontsheng lerato le kutlwelobotlhoko mme re dire Madiba motlotlo.

src: Cabinet noted the 58th anniversary of the signing of the Freedom Charter signed on the 26th June 1955 which is the foundation of our democracy and Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile segopotso sa bo 58 sa go saeniwa ga Tumelano ya Kgololesego e e leng motheo wa temokerasi le wa Molaotheo wa rona, e e saenilweng ka la bo 26 Seetebosigo 1955.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to ‘Play Your Part’ in taking the country closer to the vision of a united, non-racial, non-sexist, democratic and prosperous South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo maAforika Borweng otlhe 'Go Tshameka Karolo ya Gago' mo go atametseng naga gaufi le ponelopele ya Aforika Borwa yo o golaganeng, yo o senang tlhaolele go ya ka semorafe, yo o sa tlhaoleng ka bong, wa temokerasi le yo o tswelelang pele.

src: Cabinet welcomes the renewed commitment by the Department of Health, together with researchers, to confront issues that pose challenges to the collective efforts in the fight against HICabinet also welcomes preparations by the Department of Health to introduce a number of new interventions into existing structures which include increased awareness on HIV and AIDS, and measures to decrease the risk of HIV infection.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela maitlamo a a ntšhwafaditsweng a Lefapha la Boitekanelo mmogo le babatlisisi, a go samagana le dintlha tse di bakang dikgwetlho malebana le maiteko a a kopanetsweng mo ntweng kgatlhanong le HIGape Kabinete e amogela dipaakanyo tse di dirilweng ke Lefapha la Boitekanelo go itsese ditsereganyo tse dintšhwa di le mmalwa mo dipopegotheong tse di ntseng di le gona tse di akaretsang temoso e e oketsegileng ka ga HIV le AIDS, le dikgato tsa go fokotsa matshosetsi a go tshwaediwa ke HIKabinete e romela matshediso go latela tlhaselo e e swabisang kwa Komponeng ya Botlhe ya Ditšhabakopano kwa Mogadishu, Somalia ka la bo 19 Seetebosigo 2013, e e tlogetseng batho ba le 15 ba tlhokafetse, ba ba akaretsang maAforika Borwa a le mabedi.

src: We call on all political groups outside the political process in Somalia to renounce violence and raise their concerns with the Federal Somali Government in a constructive and reconciliatory manner.
tgt: Re ikuela mo ditlhopheng tsotlhe tsa sepolotiki tse di kwa ntle ga tsamaiso ya sepolotiki kwa Somalia go tlogela tirisodikgoka le go isa matshwenyego a tsona kwa Pusong ya BoFederale ya Somalia ka tsela e e agang le ya poelano.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to volunteer 67 minutes of their time on Nelson Mandela Day (18 July) to help change their communities and South Africa for the better.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo maAforika Borweng otlhe go ithaopa metsotso e le 67 ka Letsatsi la Nelson Mandela (18 Phukwi) go thusa go fetola baagi ba bona le Aforika Borwa go nna botoka.

src: This year’s event will take place under the theme of “Take action inspire change make every day a Mandela Day” with a focus on food security, shelter and literacy.
tgt: Tiragalo ya monongwaga e tla diragala ka moono wa "Tsaya kgato susumetsa diphetogo dira letsatsi lengwe le lengwe go nna Letsatsi la Mandela" mme go tla bo go totilwe tlhagiso e e sa tlhaeleng ya dijo tsa naga, matlo le kitso ya go buisa le go kwala.

src: Cabinet noted that as part of the Nelson Mandela Day, the phased roll-out of the Smart ID card will be launched.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile gore jaaka karolo ya Letsatsi la Nelson Mandela, katoloso e e dirwang ka dikarolo ya Karata ya Boitshupo e tla bo e tlhomiwa.

src: This launch is a significant break with our past and the end of the passbook era in South Africa.
tgt: Tlhongo eno ke kgaogano ya botlhokwa le lemorago la rona gammogo le bokhutlo jwa paka ya bukana ya pasa mo Aforika Borwa.

src: The smart ID is a contactless card with a capability to accommodate information from various stakeholders now and in future.
tgt: Karata ya Boitshupo eno ke karata e e senang dintlha tsa kgolagano e e nang le bokgoni jwa go nna le tshedimosetso go tswa kwa batsayakarolong ba ba farologaneng ga jaanong le ba mo isagong.

src: The Minister of Home Affairs will provide more details in planned briefing in due course.
tgt: Tona ya Merero ya Selegae o tla tlamela ka dintlha tse dingwe mo kopanong e e rulagantsweng mo tsamaong ya nako.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the Department of Basic Education campaign called 94+ Projects for Madiba to celebrate Nelson Mandela’s birthday and legacy.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela go tlhomiwa ga letsholo le le bidiwang Diporojeke di le 94+ ke Lefapha la Thuto ya Motheo, go keteka letsatsi la botsalo la ga Nelson Mandela mmogo le boswa jwa gagwe.

src: The campaign aims to improve infrastructure in over 94 schools to become state-of-the-art institutions of quality learning.
tgt: Maikaelelo a letsholo leno ke go tokafatsa mafaratlhatlha kwa dikolong tse di fetang 94 go di fetola go nna ditheo tsa maemo a a kwa godimo a thuto ya boleng.

src: The campaign gives hope and dignity to schools across the country.
tgt: Letsholo leno le neela dikolong go ralala naga tsholofelo le seriti.

src: During Mandela Month from July 2013, the department will be leading the handover of completed new schools per week as part of the commitment to improve quality basic education.
tgt: Mo Kgweding ya Mandela go tloga ka Phukwi 2013, lefapha, beke nngwe le nngwe, le tla bo le eteletse pele go neelana ka dikolo tse dintšhwa tse di konoseditsweng go agiwa jaaka karolo ya maitlamo a go tokafatsa thuto ya motheo ya boleng.

src: Cabinet welcomes the completion and handover of the Nkosi Dalibhunga Mandela Legacy Bridge to the Mvezo community which is led by Nkosi Mandla Mandela, grandson of former President Nelson Mandela, on 18 July 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela go konosediwa le go neelwa ga Borogo jwa Boswa jwa Kgosi Dalibhunga Mandela mo baaging ba Mveso ba ba eteletsweng pele ke Kgosi Mandla Mandela, setlogolo sa Moporesitente wa maloba Nelson Mandela, ka la bo 18 Phukwi 2013.

src: The handover will coincide with the birthday of Former President Mr Nelson Mandela, who will turn 95 years of age on this day.
tgt: Neelo eo e tla diragadiwa ka nako e le nngwe le letsatsi la botsalo la Moporesitente wa maloba Rre Nelson Mandela, yo o tla bong a gola go nna le dingwaga di le 95 ka lone letsatsi leo.

src: Cabinet noted South Africa’s commemoration of the United Nations International Day against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking on 26 June 2013, in Kimberley.
