src: Cabinet approved the hosting of the Africa Regional Seminar on the Protection of Persons based on Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression, by the South African Human Rights Commission, from 3 to 5 March 2016.The seminar will facilitate a dialogue to establish greater understanding of the root causes and manifestation of these challenges so as to find practical solutions and options available to States to address these violations.
tgt: Kabinete e eleletsa barutwana botlhe ba ba kwalang ditlhatlhobo tsa Tlaleletso tsa Setifikeiti se Segolwane/Materiki masego.

src: Cabinet wishes all learners who are writing their Supplementary Senior Certificate examination the best.
tgt: Barutwana ba rotloediwa go fitlhelela Lenaane le le sa tswang go tlhomiwa la tshegetso la tšhono ya bobedi ya materiki le le fitlhelwang kwa diporofenseng tsotlhe mme le thusa barutwana ka dithuto tsa bona ka ditlamelo tse di farologaneng.

src: Learners are encouraged to access the newly launched second chance matric support Programme which is available in all provinces and assists learners with their studies through various resources.
tgt: Maitlhomo a Lenaane la Materiki la Tšhono ya Bobedi ke go tlamela bašwa ba ba sa kgonang go fitlhelela ditlhokego tsa Setifikeiti sa Bosetšhaba se Segolwane (NSC), tšhono ya bobedi go amogela materiki mme ka go rialo ba tokafatse boleng jwa matshelo.

src: The objective of the Second Chance Matric Programme is to offer young people who have failed to meet the requirements of the National Senior Certificate (NSC) a second chance to obtain a matric thereby improving quality of life.
tgt: Ditlhatlhobo tsa tlaleletso ke karolo ya Lenaane la lefapha la Tshegetso la Tšhono ya Bobedi ya Materiki mme le naya barutwana ba ba iseng ba fitlhelele ditlhokegopotlana tsa go fetisiwa le go bona setifikeiti, ba ba tlhokang dirutwa tse pedi go fitlhelela NSC, tšhono ya go dira jalo.

src: Supplementary examinations form part of the department’s Second Chance Matric Support Programme and afford candidates that have not met the minimum promotion and certification requirements‚ but who require a maximum of two subjects to obtain a NSC an opportunity to do so.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela kitsiso ya Moporesitente ya maina a ditokololo tsa Khomišene ya Dipatlisiso ya Thuto e Kgolwane.

src: Cabinet welcomes the announcement by the President of the names of the members of the Commission of Inquiry into Higher Education.
tgt: E ikuela mo baameging botlhe ba ba nang le kgatlhego mo Thutong e Kgolwane go tshwaela mo tirong ya khomišene gore go bongwe tharabololo ya leruri ya dikgwetlho tse di lebaganeng le Thuto e Kgolwane.

src: The Minister of Mineral Resources Mosebenzi Zwane, Minister of Women in The Presidency Susan Shabangu and Minister of Social Development Bathabile Dlamini – who were appointed by President Zuma to provide support to the provincial government, mine owners and affected families following on the tragedy at the Lily Gold Mine in Barberton – briefed Cabinet on the latest developments.
tgt: Tona ya Ditlamelo tsa Dimenerale Mosebenzi Zwane, Tona kwa Lefapheng le le mo Kantorong ya Moporesitente Susan Shabangu le Tona ya Tlhabololo ya Loago Bathabile Dlamini - ba ba neng ba tlhomilwe ke Moporesitente Zuma go tlamela tshegetso go puso ya porofene, beng ba moepo mmogo le malapa a a amegileng go latela matlhotlhapelo a kwa Moepong wa Gauta wa Lily kwa Barberton - ba tlhaloseditse Kabinete dintlha tsa ga jaana.

src: Cabinet joined the President in calling on the nation to keep the three mineworkers still trapped underground and their families in our thoughts and prayers.
tgt: Kabinete e ikamantse le Moporesitente ka go ikuela mo setšhabeng go baya badiri ba moepo ba ba sa ntseng ba gaeletswe ka fa tlase ga lefatshe mmogo le bamalapa a bona mo dithapelong.

src: Cabinet remains concerned on the drought still affecting some parts of the country.
tgt: Kabinete e sa ntse e tshwentswe ke komelelo e e sa ntseng e amile dikarolo dingwe tsa naga.

src: It has expressed its gratitude to all South Africans who are supporting drought relief efforts.
tgt: E tlhagisitse ditebogo go maAforika Borwa otlhe, a a tshegetsang maiteko a namolo ya komelelo.

src: Cabinet extends its appreciation to those who have heeded the call to report any leaks in support of the War on Leaks Campaign led by Minister of Water and Sanitation Nomvula Mokonyane.
tgt: Kabinete e leboga botlhe ba ba tsibogetseng boikuelo jwa go bega go dutla go tshegetsa Letsholo la Ntwa ya go Dutla le le eteletsweng pele ke Tona ya Metsi le Bophepa Nomvula Mokonyane.

src: Cabinet appreciates the spirit of Ubuntu shown by the initiative led by Operation Hydrate that has made a difference to communities in distress.
tgt: Kabinete e itumelela mowa wa Botho/Ubuntu o o bontshitsweng ke maiteko a a eteletsweng pele ke Operation Hydrate a a dirileng pharologano mo baaging ba ba neng ba le mo tlalelong.

src: The Cabinet debated and considered the full implications of the commencement of the Taxation Laws Amendment Act, 2014.
tgt: Kabinete e ganetsane le go lebelela ditlamorago ka botlalo tsa go simolola go dirisiwa ga Molao o o Baakantsweng wa Melao ya Kgethiso, 2014.

src: In terms of that Act, the annuitisation of provident fund benefits will commence on 1 March 2016.
tgt: Go ya ka Molao, go fetolelwa ga ditshiamelo tsa letlole la tlamelo go nna tse di duelwang ka paka e e rileng go tla simolola ka la bo 1 Mopitlwe 2016.

src: That means that from that date provident fund benefits and pension fund benefits will be treated equally in that provident fund members will on retirement be permitted to take one third of their provident fund benefits in cash as a lump sum payment and the remaining two thirds of their benefits will have to be used by them to purchase annuities.
tgt: Seno se kaya gore go tloga ka letlha leo, ditshiamelo tsa letlole la tlamelo le ditshiamelo tsa letlole la phenšene di tla tsewa ka go lekalekana ka gore e tla re fa ditokololo tsa letlole la tlamelo di rola tiro di letlelelwe go tsaya nngwetharong ya ditshiamelo tsa tsona tsa letlole la tlamelo e le tuelo ya madi a a seatleng mme peditharong e e setseng ya ditshiamelo tsa bona ba tla e dirisa go reka tlamelo e e duelang madi ka paka e e rileng gongwe annuity.

src: The very same provision applies to members of pension funds currently.
tgt: Ditlamelo tseo ke tse di dirang mo ditokololong tsa matlole a phenšene ga jaana.

src: The changes in the legislation affect high-end earners and all other persons who belong to provident funds.
tgt: Diphetogo tsa molao di ama baamogedi ba ba kwa godimo mmogo le batho botlhe ba e leng ditokololo tsa matlole a tlamelo.

src: A number of organisations and individuals have expressed concern about the implementation of the new changes and have made representations to the government about the implementation.
tgt: Ditheo di le mmalwa le batho ba tlhagisitse matshwenyego ka go tsenngwa tirisong ga diphetogo tse dintšhwa mme ba dirile ditlhagiso kwa pusong malebana le go tsenngwa tirisong.

src: It is apparent that despite the extensive consultation processes which were embarked upon before the law was passed that those concerns still exist and that those concerns have to be addressed urgently to ensure that when the law commences the changes to the provident fund benefits will be implemented smoothly and efficiently.
tgt: Go bonala gore le fa go nnile le thulaganyo e e tseneletseng ya patlomaikutlo e e dirilweng pele ga molao o ka fetisiwa, matshwenyego ao a sa ntse a le gona le gore go tshwanetse ga samaganwa le matshwenyego ao pele ka bonako go netefatsa gore fa molao o simolola go dira, diphetogo tsa ditshiamelo tsa letlole la tlamelo di tla diragadiwa sentle kwa ntle ga kgoreletsego.

src: For that reason, Cabinet has decided to table a legislative amendment to the Taxation Laws Amendment Act as a matter of urgency to postpone the commencement date from 1 March 2016 to 1 March 2018 to allow for further consultations with all key stakeholders.
tgt: Ka ntlha ya seo, Kabinete e sweditse go tlhagisa paakanyo ya molao ya Molao wa Paakanyo ya Melao ya Kgethiso e le ntlha e e akofileng go busetsa morago letlha la tshimologo go tloga go la bo 1 Mopitlwe 2016 go ya go la bo 1 Mopitlwe 2018 go letla gore go nne le patlomaikutlo ya baamegi ba botlhokwa gape.

src: Those consultations may result in further amendment to the laws.
tgt: Patlomaikutlo eno e ka baka gore go nne le paakanyo e nngwe ya melao.

src: An Amendment Bill will be tabled in Parliament within the next few days.
tgt: Molaotlhomo wa Paakanyo o tla tlhagisiwa mo Palamenteng mo malatsing a se kae a a latelang.

src: Cabinet conveys condolences on the recent passing away of His Grace Bishop Glayton Modise of the International Pentecostal Holiness Church.
tgt: Kabinete e romela matshediso ka ntlha ya go tlhokafala fa gautshwane ga Moitshepi Bishopo Glayton Modise wa Kereke ya International Pentecostal Holiness Church.

src: Bishop Modise led the congregation with over three million members across southern Africa, following the death of his father and the founder of the church, His Grace Comforter Frederick Modise in 1996.
tgt: Bishopo Modise o eteletse pele phuthego ya ditokololo tse di fetang dimilione di le tharo go ralala borwa jwa Aforika, go latela go tlhokafala ga ga rraagwe le mosimolodi wa kereke, Moitshepi Comforter Frederick Modise ka 1996.

src: Cabinet also conveys its deepest sympathies on the recent passing away of the former Secretary-General of the United Nations (UN) Chief Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
tgt: Gape kabinete e romela matshediso malebana le go tlhokafala ga Mokwaledi-Kakaretso wa maloba wa Ditšhabakopano (UN) Kgosi Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

src: He took office in 1992 at the time of growing influence for the UN following its decisive role in the Gulf war, serving one five year term.
tgt: O tsene mo kantorong ka 1992 ka nako ya fa tshusumetso ya UN e ne e gola go latela seabe sa botlhokwa kwa ntweng ya Kgokgometso, mme a dira paka e le nngwe ya dingwaga tse tlhano.

src: He died at a Cairo hospital on Tuesday aged He will be remembered for his contribution to peace and democracy.
tgt: O tlhokafaletse kwa sepetlele sa Cairo ka Labobedi a na le dingwaga tse O tla gakologelwa ka tshwaelo ya gagwe mo kagisong le temokerasi.

src: Cabinet congratulates Mr Kevin Govender from the Cape Town-based Office of Astronomy for Development and the International Astronomical Union who will be jointly awarded the prestigious Edinburgh Medal for 2016 for establishing the Office of Astronomy for Development in Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola Rre Kevin Govender wa Kantoro ya Motsekapa ya Bolepanaledi go lebeletswe Tlhabololo mmogo le Mokgatlho wa Boditšhabatšhaba wa Bolepanaledi yo a tla abelwang mmogo Metale o o Tlotlegang wa Edinburgh wa 2016 ka ntlha ya go tlhoma Kantoro ya Bolepanaledi go lebeletswe Tlhabololo kwa Motsekapa.

src: Govender is the first South African to receive this prestigious award for science and technology achievements which contribute to the understanding and well-being of humanity.
tgt: Govender ke moAforika Borwa wa ntlha go amogela sekgele seno se se tlotlegang sa diphitlhelelo tsa saense le thekenoloji e e tshwaelang mo go tlhaloganyeng le itekanelong ya batho.

src: Cabinet commends 16-year-old ballet dancer Leroy Mokgatle who won an Audience Favourite award and a scholarship at the Prix de Lausanne International Ballet Competition in Switzerland.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola motantshi wa dingwaga di le 16 wa ballet, Leroy Mokgatle yo a gapileng sekgele sa Audience Favourite mmogo le sekolašipi kwa Kgaisanong ya Boditšhabatšhaba ya Ballet ya Pris de Lausanne kwa Switzerland.

src: He is the first South African to win this scholarship in 28 years and the second in the country’s history.
tgt: Ke moAforika Borwa wa ntlha go gapa sekolašipi mo dingwageng di le 28 le wa bobedi mo hisetoring ya naga.

src: Cabinet joins President Zuma in applauding the winners of the 2nd Annual Ubuntu Awards.
tgt: Kabinete e ikamanya le Moporesitente Zuma go akgola bafenyi ba Dikgele tsa bo 2 tsa Ngwaga le ngwaga tsa Ubuntu.

src: These awards recognise South African industry leaders and eminent persons for their contribution to promote our national interests and values across the globe.
tgt: Dikgele tseno di akgola baeteledipele ba indaseteri ba Aforika Borwa mmogo le batho ba ba tlhagelelang ka ntlha ya ditshwaelo tsa bona go tsweletsa dikgatlhego tsa rona tsa bosetšhaba mmogo le dintlhatheo tsa maitsholo a rona go ralala lefatshe.

src: Cabinet congratulates flautist Wouter Kellerman, cappella group Ladysmith Black Mambazo and gospel singer Neville D for their 2016 Grammy nominations.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola flautist Wouter Kellerman, setlhopha sa cappella Ladysmith Black Mambazo le moopedi wa mmino wa sedumedi Neville D ka ntlha ya go supiwa mo dikgeleng tsa Grammy tsa 2016.

src: These artists are an inspiration and hold the South African flag high.
tgt: Batsweretshi bano ba a rotloetsa e bile ba fofisetsa folaga ya Aforika Borwa kwa godimo tota.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: Go thapiwaGo thapiwa gotlhe go tla diragadiwa fa makwalothuto otlhe a netefaditswe mme go amogetswe tetlelelo e e matshwanedi:.

src: Lepelle Northern Water Board:a) His Majesty Thovhele Tshivhase (Chairperson)b) Mr Matsebe Ivor Phasha (Deputy Chairperson)c) Ms Thandeka Thembekile Celiwe Hlongwa (member)d) Mr Boxing Phillemon Sebola (member)e) Mr Ntale Herold Matsepe (member)f) Ms Mankone Mabataung Ntsaba (member)g) Ms L Malamba (member)h) Ms Josephine Mampheri Letsoalo (member) andi) Ms Makgetsi Annabelle Mphahlele (member).
tgt: Boto ya Metsi ya Borwa jwa Lepelle:a) Motlotlegi Thovhele Tshivhase (Modulasetilo)b) Rre Matsebe Ivor Phasha (Motlatsamodulasetilo)c) Mme Thandeka Thembekile Celiwe Hlongwa (tokololo)d) Rre Boxing Phillemon Sebola (tokololo)e) Rre Ntale Herold Matsepe (tokololo)f) Mme Mankone Mabataung Ntsaba (tokololo)g) Mme L Malamba (tokololo)h) Mme Josephine Mampheri Letsoalo (tokololo) lei) Mme Makgetsi Annabelle Mphahlele (tokololo).

src: Implementation of key government programmes.
tgt: Go tsenngwa tirisong ga manaaneo a botlhokwa a puso.

src: Cabinet welcomed the 2016 Budget Speech delivered by Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan on 24 February 2016.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse Puo ya Tekanyetsokabo ya 2016 e e dirilweng ke Tona ya Ditšhelete Pravin Gordhan ka la bo 24 Tlhakole 2016.

src: This budget demonstrates our resilience, commitment and resourcefulness as we navigate through this worst economic period in recent history.
tgt: Tekanyetsokabo eno e bontsha go tsetsepela ga rona, maitlamo a rona mmogo le mosola wa rona fa re ntse re samagane le paka eno e e maswe go gaisa ya ikonomi mo ya mo malobeng.

src: The budget responds to what the country needs and creates confidence in the economy by placing the country on a credible, sustainable and viable inclusive economic growth path.
tgt: Tekanyetsokabo e tsibogela se naga e se tlhokang mme e dira gore go nne le boikanyego mo ikonoming ka go baya naga mo tseleng e e ikanyegang, ya leruri le e e ka diregang mme e akaretsa ya kgolo ya ikonomi.

src: Cabinet further welcomes the decisive cost-containment measures and commits to working together with all sectors in contributing towards a collective national effort to implement the course set by the budget.
tgt: Gape kabinete e amogela dikgato tsa botlhokwa tsa go fokotsa ditshenyegelo mme e itlama go dira mmogo le maphata otlhe go tshwaela mo maitekong a a tlhakanetsweng a bosetšhaba a go diragatsa kgato eno e e tlhomilweng ke tekanyetsokabo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the Presidential Press Corps (PPC) by President Jacob Zuma.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela go tlhomiwa ga Setlhopha sa Bobegakgang sa Moporesitente (PPC) ke Moporesitente Jacob Zuma.

src: The PPC will comprise political editors, political correspondents, political reporters and economics journalists who have been accredited to cover The Presidency on a full-time and ongoing basis.
tgt: PPC e tla akaretsa batseleganyi ba dikgang tsa sepolotiki, bakwaladikgang ba sepolotiki, babegakgang ba dipolotiki mmogo le babegakgang ba ikonomi ba ba tlhomamisitsweng go bega dikgang tsa Kantoro ya Moporesitente ka dinako tsotlhe.

src: The purpose of the PPC is to provide improved access to information by the media.
tgt: Maitlhomo a PPC ke go tlamela bobegakgang ka phitlhelesego e e tokafaditsweng ya tshedimosetso.

src: It will also improve access by the media to the President and The Presidency, in order to ensure that journalists also obtain background information and processes to enhance their understanding and reporting.
tgt: Gape e tla tokafatsa go fitlhelesega ga Moporesitente le Kantoro ya Moporesitente mo bobegakgannyeng go netefatsa gore babegakgang ba amogela tshedimosetso ya lemorago le dithulaganyo go tokafatsa go tlhaloganya le go bega ga bona.

src: The press core members will also receive briefings from the Deputy President and any Minister that the President invites to share programmes of national importance.
tgt: Ditokololo tsa setlhopha sa bobegakgang di tla amogela dipego go tswa go Motlatsamoporesitente le Tona nngwe le nngwe e Moporesitente a e laletsang go arogana manaane a botlhokwa a bosetšhaba.

src: Cabinet has expressed appreciation of the contribution that South Africa has made towards restoring peace in Burundi, in line with our foreign policy commitments to ensure a peaceful and stable WEBTOKEN further welcomed the outcomes of the inclusive Inter-Burundian Dialogue held during the visit by the African Union (AU) high-level delegation of Heads of State and Government to Bujumbura in Burundi, which was led by President Zuma.
tgt: Kabinete e tlhagisitse ditebogo ka ntlha ya karolo eo Aforika Borwa e nnileng le yona malebana le go busetsa kagiso kwa Burundi, go lepalepana le maitlamo a rona a dipholisi tsa dinaga di sele go netefatsa gore go nna le kontinente e e renang kagiso e bile e tsepame.

src: Cabinet welcomes the appointment of President Zuma by the United Nations (UN) Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon, to co-chair a High-Level Commission on Health Employment and Economic Growth with President François Hollande of the Republic of France.
tgt: Gape e amogetse dipoelo tsa Puisano e e akaretsang ya ka fa gare ga Burundi e e neng e tshwerwe ka nako ya leeto la kemedi ya maemo a a kwa godimo ya Mokgatlhotshwaraganelo wa Aforika (AU), e e neng e eteletswe pele ke Moporesitente Zuma.

src: This is not the first time that President Zuma has been appointed by a world body to undertake work at a global stage.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela go thapiwa ga Moporesitente Zuma ke Mokwaledikakaretso wa Ditšhabakopano (UN) Ban Ki-moon, go tlhakanela bodulasetilo jwa Khomišene ya Maemo a a kwa Godimo ya Boitekanelo, Ditiro le Kgolo ya Ikonomi le Moporesitente François Hollande wa Rephaboliki ya France.

src: This appointment is in recognition of the sterling leadership displayed by our President in the international arena.
tgt: Ga se la ntlha Moporesitente Zuma a thapiwa ke setheo sa lefatshe go dira tiro mo seraleng sa lefatshe.

src: The commission will stimulate the creation of new employment opportunities in the health sector across all countries, especially in least developed ones.
tgt: Khomišene e tla susumetsa go tlhamiwa ga ditšhono tsa ditiro tse dintšhwa mo lephateng la boitekanelo go ralala dinaga tsotlhe, bogolo segolo tse di sa tlhabologang mo go kalo.

src: This also strengthens the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, which will go a long way to addressing the triple challenge of unemployment, poverty and inequality.
tgt: Gape seno se maatlafatsa go diragadiwa ga Lenaane la 2030 la Tlhabololo e e nnelang leruri, e leng se se tla thusang go samagana le dikgwetlho tse di maphata mararo a botlhokatiro, lehuma le go tlhoka tekatekano.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the 2016 National Community Survey in Mamelodi, Pretoria by the Minister in The Presidency Jeff Radebe and the Statistician-General Pali Lehohla.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela go tlhomiwa ga Tshekatsheko ya Bosetšhaba ya Baagi ya 2016 kwa Mamelodi, Pretoria ke Tona mo Kantorong ya Moporesitente Jeff Radebe le Radipalopalokakaretso Pali Lehohla.

src: This year’s survey is being undertaken under the theme: “The South African I know, the home I understand” and is targeting more than 1,5 million households – the biggest so far compared to the one held five years ago that sampled only 300 000 households.
tgt: Tshekatsheko ya monongwaga e dirwa ka fa tlase ga moono wa: "MoAforika Borwa yo ke mo itseng, legae le ke le tlhaloganyang" mme go totilwe magae a feta 1,5 milione - e leng palo e kgolo go gaisa fa e bapisiwa le e e neng e totilwe mo dingwageng di le tlhano tse di fetileng mo go neng go dirilwe tshekatsheko ya magae a le 300 000 fela.

src: The survey will be undertaken in April and the results made available by the end of June 2016.
tgt: Tshekatsheko e tla dirwa ka Moranang mme dipholo di tla itsesewe kwa bokhutlong jwa Seetebosigo 2016.

src: Cabinet notes with concern the report presented by the World Health Organisation and the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development to the Health Market Enquiry headed by Justice Sandile Ngcobo.
tgt: Kabinete e nopotse ke go tshwenngwa ke pegelo e e tlhagisitsweng ke Mokgatlho wa Lefatshe wa Boitekanelo (WHO) le Mokgatlho wa Tirisanommogo ya Ikonomi le Tlhabololo mo Patlisisong ya Mmaraka wa Boitekanelo e e eteletsweng pele ke Moatlhodi Sandile Ngcobo.

src: The reports indicate that South Africa provides the most expensive medical services when compared with other countries.
tgt: Pegelo e supa gore Aforika Borwa e tlamela ka ditirelo tsa kalafi tse di tlhotlhwagodimo go gaisa fa e bapisiwa le dinaga tse dingwe.

src: Cabinet will await the conclusion of the enquiry before pronouncing on this matter.
tgt: Kabinete e tla emela go konosediwa ga patlisiso pele ga go dira kgoeletso ka morero ono.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the Draft Strategy for Addressing Air Pollution in Dense Low-Income Communities of South Africa for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse go phasaladiwa ga Togamaanotlhomo ya go Samagana le Kgotlhelego ya Mowa mo Baaging ba Lotseno lo lo kwa tlase ba ba nnang mo go kitlaneng gona mo Aforika Borwa gore go dirwe ditshwaelo.

src: The strategy seeks to provide a dedicated focused approach to deal with high levels of pollution in some of the densely populated low-income communities.
tgt: Maikaelelo a togamaano ke go tlamela ka tsela e e tsepameng go samagana le seelo se se kwa godimo sa kgotlhelego mo baaging bangwe ba ba bonang lotseno lo lo kwa tlase mme ba nna mo go kitlaneng gona.

src: It provides a coordinated approach to the implementation of efforts to reduce domestic fuel burning.
tgt: E tlamela ka tsela e e gokaganeng ya go tsenngwa tirisong ga maiteko a go fokotsa go fisa dituki mo magaeng.

src: The intervention is to ensure these areas comply with the National Ambient Air Quality Standards.
tgt: Tsereganyo eno e ikaelela go netefatsa gore dikarolo tseno di obamela Seemo sa Bosetšhaba sa Boleng jwa Mowa wa Tikologo.

src: This focused strategy will support the existing national strategy to address air pollution in the country.
tgt: Togamaano eno e e tsepameng e tla tshegetsa togamaano e e leng teng ya bosetšhaba ya go samagana le kgotlhelego ya mowa mo nageng.

src: Cabinet approved the co-hosting of the 21st International AIDS Conference (AIDS 2016) between government and the International AIDS Society at the International Convention Centre (ICC) in Durban from 18 to 22 July 2016.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse go amogelwa ga Khonferense ya bo 21 ya Boditšhabatšhaba ya AIDS (AIDS 2016) ke puso le Mokgatlho wa Boditšhabatšhaba wa AIDS kwa International Convention Centre (ICC) kwa Durban go tloga ka la bo 18 go fitlha ka la bo 22 Phukwi 2016.

src: Hosting the conference will advance our country’s HIV and tuberculosis response whilst impacting on one of the most important challenges in South Africa, the region and the world.
tgt: Go amogela khonferense go tla tokafatsa tsibogo ya naga ya rona ya HIV le TB fa go ntse go ama nngwe ya dikgwetlho tsa botlhokwa tota mo Aforika Borwa, mo kgaolong le mo lefatsheng.

src: This conference will provide a platform for researchers from across the world to share the latest scientific advances in the field, to learn from one another’s expertise and to develop strategies for advancing all facets of our collective efforts to treat and prevent HIBill.
tgt: Khonferense eno e tla naya babatlisisi go tswa lefatsheng ka bophara serala sa go arogana dikgatelopele tsa ga jaana tsa saense mo lephateng, go ithuta mo boitseanapeng jwa ba bangwe mmogo le go tlhama maano a go tsweletsa dikarolo tsotlhe tsa maiteko a re a tlhakanetseng a go alafa le go thibela HIMolaotlhomo.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the National Land Transport Amendment Bill of 2015 to Parliament, which amends the National Land Transport Act, 2009 (Act 5 of 2009).
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse tlhagiso ya Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa 2015 wa Dipalangwa tsa Bosetšhaba tsa mo Lefatsheng, o o baakanyang Molao wa Bosetšhaba wa Dipalangwa tsa mo Lefatsheng, 2009 (Molao wa bo 5 wa 2009).

src: The amendments to the National Land Transport Act of 2009 will further the process of transforming and restructuring the national land transport system.
tgt: Dipaakanyo tsa Molao wa Bosetšhaba wa Dipalangwa tsa mo Lefatsheng wa 2009 di tla tsweletsa thulaganyo ya go fetola le go aga sešwa thulaganyo ya bosetšhaba ya dipalangwa tsa mo lefatsheng.

src: This will contribute towards a safer, accessible, efficient and effective public transport service.
tgt: Seno se tla tshwaela mo tirelong ya dipalangwa tsa botlhe e e babalesegileng, e e fitlhelesegang mme e le bokgoni.

src: The Bill provides for new developments in the public transport sector.
tgt: Molaotlhomo o dira tlamelo ya ditlhabololo tse dintšhwa mo lephateng la dipalangwa tsa botlhe.

src: The Bill provides guidance in, amongst others, non-motorised transport e-hailing transport services and branding of public transport.
tgt: Molaotlhomo o tlamela ka kaedi ya, magareng ga tse dingwe, dipalangwa tse di senang dienjene, ditirelo tsa dipalangwa tse di bidiwang ka tiriso ya diselefounu gongwe dikhomphiutara mmogo le go tshwaya dipalangwa tsa botlhe.

src: It further provides administrative clarity on the delegated powers and regulations in respect of the issuing of public transport operating licenses.
tgt: Gape o sedimosa ntlha ya tsamaiso malebana le dithata tse di roletsweng mmogo le melawana malebana le go rebolwa ga dilaesense tsa go dira tsa dipalangwa tsa botlhe.

src: This Bill will also enable the roll-out of the Integrated Public Transport Networks and it forms part of the National Infrastructure Plan and the Strategic Integrated Project 7, which focus on using coordinated development of urban and integrated transport networks to establish cities as engines of growth.
tgt: Gape molaotlhomo ono o tla kgontsha go anamisiwa ga Mafaratlhatlha a a Lotaneng a Dipalangwa tsa Botlhe mme ke karolo ya Leano la Bosetšhaba la Mafaratlhatlha le Porojeke ya Togamaano e e Lotaneng ya 7 e e totileng go dirisa tlhabololo e e gokaganeng ya mafaratlhatlha a a lotaneng a dipalangwa go dira gore ditoropokgolo e nne madutelo a kgolo ya ikonomi.

src: Upcoming events President Zuma will undertake a State Visit to the Federal Republic of Nigeria from 8 to 9 March 2016.
tgt: Moporesitente Zuma o tla tsaya Leeto la Semmuso go ya kwa Rephaboliking ya Bofederale ya Nigeria go tloga ka la bo 8 go fitlha ka la bo 9 Mopitlwe 2016.

src: The State Visit will enhance existing bilateral relations and further advance intra-regional trade.
tgt: Leeto la Semmuso le tla tokafatsa dikamano tsa ga jaana tsa sebedi le go tsweletsa gape kgwebisano ya mo kgaolong.

src: Human Rights Month in March 2016 will be celebrated under the theme: “South Africa united against racism.” The Department of Arts and Culture has put in place a month-long programme which includes a series of dialogues on working together to build a non-racial, non-sexist, equal and democratic society.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Ditshwanelo tsa Botho ka Mopitlwe 2016 e tla ketekwa ka fa tlase ga moono wa: "Aforika Borwa e kopane kgatlhanong le tlhaolele ya bosemorafe."

src: Cabinet invites South Africans to comment on the National Action Plan to combat Racism, Racial Discrimination, Xenophobia and Related Intolerance (2016-2021) before 30 June 2016.
tgt: Lefapha la Botsweretshi le Setso le rulagantse leano la kgwedi le le akaretsang metseletsele ya dipuisano tse di ka ga go dira mmogo go aga setšhaba se se sa tlhaoleng go ya ka bosemorafe, bong, se se nang le tekatekano le sa temokerasi.

src: The plan provides the basis for a public policy against racial discrimination that will assist in giving effect to our international human rights obligations.
tgt: Kabinete e laletsa maAforika Borwa go tshwaela mo Leanotirong la Bosetšhaba la go lwantsha Bosemorafe, Tlhaolo go ya ka Bosemorafe, Letlhoo la Batswakwantle mmogo le Go tlhoka itshokelano go go Amanang le tseo (2016-2021) pele ga la bo 30 Seetebosigo 2016.

src: The conference is a follow-up session of the Russia-Africa Anti-Drug Dialogue, which aims to present a consolidated position in how world leaders intend to tackle the international drug problem.
tgt: Leano le tlamela ka motheo wa pholisi ya botlhe e e kgatlhanong le go tlhaola go ya ka bosemorafe e e tla thusang go diragatsa maitlamo a rona a boditšhabatšhaba a ditshwanelo tsa botho.

src: Government – in partnership with the Commonwealth Secretariat, University of South Africa (UNISA) and the National Youth Development Agency – is hosting the 2nd Commonwealth Conference on Youth Work at the UNISA campus in Pretoria from 8 to 10 March 2016.
tgt: Puisano ya Russia-Aforika e e Kgatlhanong le Diritibatsi kwa ICC kwa Durban go tloga ka la bo 8 go fitlha ka la bo 9 Mopitlwe 2016 e tlamela ka serala sa go tokafatsa Leanolegolo la Bosetšhaba la Diritibatsi (2013-2017)Ntwa kgatlhanong le diritibatsi tse di seng mo molaong go lepalepana le Leano la Tlhabololo la Bosetšhaba (NDP) mme puisano e ka fa tlase ga bookamedi jwa AU go latelelwa maitlamo go ya ka Ditumelano tse di maleba tsa UN tsa Bosenyi jo bo Rulagantsweng go ralala Dinaga, Leano la Tiragatso la AU la Taolo ya Diritibatsi (2013-2017) le ditshwetso tsa BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China le Aforika Borwa).Khonferense ke kopano e e latelang Puisano ya Russia-Aforika e e Kgatlhanong le Diritibatsi, e maikaelelo a yona e leng go tlhagisa seemo se se gokaganeng malebana le gore baeteledipele ba lefatshe ba ikaelela go samagana jang le bothata jwa boditšhabatšhaba jwa diritibatsi.

src: The conference takes place under the theme: “Engaging Young People in Nation Building: The Youth Worker’s Role” and will re-examine the role of youth work practitioners and academics in engaging young people on the development of their countries.
tgt: Khonferense e tshwarwa ka fa tlase ga moono wa: "Go akaretsa Bašwa mo Kagong ya Setšhaba: Seabe sa Modiri wa Mošwa" mme e tla sekaseka gape seabe sa badiri ba tiro ya bašwa mmogo le barutegi ba ba akaretsang bašwa mo tlhabololong ya dinaga tsa bona.

src: Cabinet’s position on key issues in the environment Cabinet reiterates the message by President Zuma on the need to respect the institutions and processes created in terms of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996 and the law.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa molaetsa wa ga Moporesitente Zuma wa botlhokwa jwa go tlotla ditheo le ditsamaiso tse di tlhamilweng go ya ka Molaotheo wa Rephaboliki ya Aforika Borwa wa 1996 le molao.

src: President Zuma is dealing with the matter of the South African Revenue Service Commissioner and the Minister of Finance through the correct channels using correct legal prescripts.
tgt: Moporesitente Zuma o samagane le morero wa Mokhomišinara wa Tirelo ya Lekgetho ya Aforika Borwa le Tona ya Ditšhelete ka tsela e e siameng a dirisa ditsela tse di siameng tsa molao.

src: The President is putting measures in place to address the issues responsibly and amicably for the benefit of all.
tgt: Moporesitente o baakanya dikgato tsa go samagana le dintlha tseno ka maikarabelo le ka tsela e e siameng gore botlhe ba bone molemo.

src: Cabinet calls on all interested parties to exercise calm and restraint, and allow space for the matters to be resolved using correct channels.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo maphateng otlhe a a nang le dikgatlhego go diga makgwafo le go itshwara mme ba neele sebaka sa gore morero ono o rarabololwe ka go dirisiwa ga ditsela tse di siameng.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to register for the 2016 Local Government Elections on 5 and 6 March 2016.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo maAforika Borweng otlhe go ikwadisetsa Ditlhopho tsa Pusoselegae tsa 2016 ka la bo 5 le la bo 6 Mopitlwe 2016.

src: Unlike with national elections, the local government elections require that you register in the ward that you reside WEBTOKEN is important to have an Identity Document (ID) – both the green bar-coded ID and Smart ID card will be accepted – and to check your registration status, ward number and voting-station location.
tgt: Go botlhokwa gore o nne le Lekwaloitshupo (ID) - go tla amogelwa ID e e tala e e nang le bar-code mmogo le karata ya Boitshupo - le go tlhola seemo sa gago sa ikwadiso, nomoro ya oto kwa diteišeneng tse di farologaneng tsa ditlhopho.

src: All Home Affairs offices will be open from 08:00 to 17:00 on 5 and 6 March 2016, which is in line with the operating hours of the Independent Electoral Commission for the two days.
tgt: Dikantoro tsotlhe tsa Merero ya Selegae di tla bo di butswe go tloga ka 08:00 go fitlha ka 17:00 ka la bo 5 le la bo 6 Mopitlwe 2016, mme seo ke go lepalepana le diura tsa tiro tsa Khomišene ya Ditlhopho e e Ikemetseng (IEC) mo matsatsing a mabedi ao.

src: Cabinet calls on all young and first-time voters to register to vote.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo batlhophing botlhe ba bašwa mmogo le ba ba tla bong ba tlhopha la ntlha go ikwadisetsa go tlhopha.

src: By casting your vote you have taken a step towards making your voice heard in the decisions that affect you and your community.
tgt: Ka go tlhopha o tsaya kgato ya go dira gore lentswe la gago le utlwale mo ditshwetsong tse di go amang le tse di amang baagi ba gaeno.

src: Local government is in your hands!.
tgt: Pusoselegae e mo diatleng tsa gago!.

src: Cabinet condemns the violent student protests, which have disrupted studies at some universities and led to the destruction of property.
tgt: Kabinete e nyefola ditshupetso tse di tletseng tirisodikgoka tsa baithuti, tse di kgoreleditseng dithuto kwa diyunibesithi tse dingweng mme di lebisitse kwa tshenyong ya dithoto.

src: These protests deprive deserving students the opportunity to further their studies and impacts upon their right to higher education.
tgt: Ditshupetso tseno di lomeletsa baithuti ba ba nang le tshiamelo tšhono ya go tsweletsa dithuto mme gape di ama tshwanelo ya bone ya go iponela thuto e kgolwane.

src: Government has opened channels of communication with all higher-education stakeholders for discussions and dialogues.
tgt: Puso e buletse dipuisano le baamegi botlhe ba thuto e kgolwane go buisana le go ganetsana.

src: This has resulted in the restoration of normality and the promotion of social cohesion in our universities that seeks to find solutions to the medium- to long-term challenges linked to the transformation of the sector as described in the resolutions of the 2015 Higher Education Transformation Summit.
tgt: Seno se buseditse maemo sekeng le tsweletso ya kgolagano ya loago kwa diyunibesithing tse di batlang go bona ditharabololo tsa dikgwetlho tsa pakagare le pakatelele tse di amanang le go fetolwa ga lephata jaaka go tlhalositswe mo ditshwetsong tsa Samiti ya 2015 ya Diphetogo mo Thutong e Kgolwane.

src: Cabinet supports the efforts by law-enforcement agencies to ensure that the culture of learning is restored, and that property and the rights of individuals are protected.
tgt: Kabinete e tshegetsa maiteko a ditheo tsa tiragatso ya molao go netefatsa gore go busediwa setso sa go ithuta, le gore go sirelediwa dithoto le ditshwanelo tsa batho.

src: The rule of law is paramount and should be upheld at all times.
tgt: Molao o botlhokwa mme o tshwanetse go tlotlwa ka dinako tsotlhe.

src: Normality and calm must return in our universities so that the academic programmes can continue while the medium- to long-term challenges are addressed.
tgt: Go tshwanetse ga busediwa maemo sekeng kwa diyunibesithing tsa rona gore manaane a thuto a tswelele pele fa go ntse go samaganwe le dikgwetlho tsa pakagare le pakatelele.

src: Cabinet applauded the students who stood united against racism and anti-white chauvinism, which serves as an example that we can all work together to build on the progress and gains made in the tertiary education sector in preparation for this academic year.
tgt: Kabinete e akgotse baithuti ba ba emeng mmogo kgatlhanong le bosemorafe le letlhoo la basweu, e leng sekai sa gore re ka dira mmogo go agelela mo tswelelopeleng le diphitlhelelong tse di dirilweng mo lephateng la thuto e kgolwane go baakanyetsa ngwaga ono wa dithuto.

src: We must protect that progress and allow order to be restored and preserved at all our universities.
tgt: Re tshwanetse go sireletsa tswelelopele eo le go letla gore go busediwe le go somarela taolo kwa diyunibesithing tsotlhe tsa rona.

src: Cabinet also calls upon all stakeholders to work together so that our universities become leaders of inclusive engagement and transformation.
tgt: Gape kabinete e ikuela mo baameging botlhe go dira mmogo gore diyunibesithi tsa rona e nne baeteledipele ba puisano e e akaretsang le diphetogo.

src: Cabinet notes the proposed merger of three bottling operations for the Coca Cola Company in South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e nopotse kgolagano e e tshitshintsweng ya ditheo tse tharo tsa mabotlolo tsa Setlamo sa Coca Cola mo Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet notes the matter will be heard before the Competition Tribunal.
tgt: Kabinete e lemoga gore morero o tla reediwa kwa Lekgotleng la Dikgaisano.

src: Cabinet expresses its concern at proposed job losses and reduction in employment in merger transactions.
tgt: Kabinete e tlhagisa matshwenyego a yona ka tatlhegelo ya ditiro e e tshitshintsweng mmogo le phokotso ya ditiro mo dikgatong tsa kgolagano eno.

src: In view of the high levels of unemployment, Cabinet calls on companies to ensure jobs are not lost and aggregate employment levels are maintained.
tgt: Ka ntlha ya botlhokatiro jo bo kwa godimo, Kabinete e ikuela mo ditlamong go netefatsa gore ga go nne le ditiro tse di latlhegang mme go tsholwa seemo sa ditiro.

src: Cabinet congratulates the South African Ambassador to the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Mr Xavier Carim, who has been elected to chair the Dispute Settlement Body of the WTO General Council.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola Moambasadara wa Aforika Borwa wa Mokgatlho wa Lefatshe wa Kgwebisano (WTO), Rre Xavier Carim, yo o tlhophilweng modulasetilo wa Setheo sa Tharabololo ya Dikgotlhang sa Lekgotlakakaretso la WTLekgotlakakaretso ke setheo se se tsayang ditshwetso tse di kwa godimo sa WTO magareng ga Dikhonferense tsa Ditona.

src: The appointment of Ambassador Carim is in part recognition of the important role South Africa plays in the WTO and in part testimony to Ambassador Carim’s qualities.
tgt: Go thapiwa ga Moambasadara Carim go lemosa seabe sa botlhokwa sa Aforika Borwa mo WTO mme gape ke sesupo sa maitshwaro a ga Moambasadara Carim.

src: Cabinet noted Barclays PLC’s announcement of its intention to reduce its per cent shareholding in Barclays Africa Group Limited (BAGL) over the next two to three years.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile kitsiso ya Barclays PLC ya maikaelelo a yona go fokotsa 62.3% ya botsholadišere jwa yona mo Barclays Africa Group Limited (BAGL) mo dingwageng tse di latelang di le pedi go ya go di le tharo.

src: Barclays PLC, in particular the CEO, has engaged both the National Treasury and the Reserve Bank in an open dialogue, and we welcome the company’s commitment to implement its new strategy in a way that will minimise the impact on the economies in which BAGL operates.
tgt: Barclays PLC, bogolosegolo Motlhankedikhuduthamagamogolo, o buisane le Matlotlo a Bosetšhaba le Bankakgolo ya Aforika Borwa mme re amogela maitlamo a setlamo a go diragatsa togamaano e ntšhwa ka tsela e e tla fokotsang ditlamorago mo ikonoming e BAGL e dirang mo go yona.

src: The Reserve Bank will work with Barclays PLC and BAGL to ensure that any potential risks from the transaction are mitigated and appropriate measures will be taken to manage capital flows arising from the transaction.
tgt: Bankakgolo ya Aforika Borwa e tla dira le Barclays PLC le BAGL go netefatsa gore go fokodiwa matshosetsi otlhe a a ka nnang teng mo tiragatsong eo le gore go tsewa dikgato tse di maleba go samagana le motsamao wa ditšhelete o o tla bakwang ke tiragatso eo.

src: Cabinet salutes all the finalists and winners of the National Teaching Awards which took place on 27 February 2016.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola botlhe ba ba fitlheletseng makgaolakgang mmogo le bafenyi ba Dikgele tsa Bosetšhaba tsa Barutabana tse di neng di tshwerwe ka la bo 27 Tlhakole 2016.

src: These dedicated teachers move our country forward by ensuring that their classrooms produce motivated learners that will contribute towards the development of South Africa.
tgt: Barutabana bano ba ba ititeileng sehuba ba tsweletsa naga ya rona pele ka go netefatsa gore diphaposiborutelo di tlhagisa barutwana ba ba rotloetsegileng ba ba tla tshwaelang mo tlhabololong ya Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet congratulates the Market Theatre in Johannesburg for celebrating its 40th year of existence.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola Market Theatre kwa Johannesburg ka go keteka ngwaga wa bo 40 e ntse e le teng.

src: During the apartheid era the theatre became a symbol of the Struggle by telling the true South African story.
tgt: Ka paka ya tlhaolele teatere e nnile sekao sa Kgaratlho ka go anela dikgang tsa boammaaruri tsa Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet congratulates music teacher, Mr Chad Hendricks, from Retreat in the Cape Flats for winning the prestigious Len van Zyl Conductors’ Competition in Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola morutabana wa mmino, Rre Chad Hendricks, go tswa kwa Retreat kwa Cape Flats ka ntlha ya go fenya Kgaisano ya maemo ya Batshwaratakata ya Len van Zyl kwa Motsekapa.

src: His prize includes a three-month United States scholarship during which Mr Hendricks will study at the Philadelphia Orchestra and be trained by renowned Profssor Victor Yampolsky in Chicago.
tgt: Dimpho tsa gagwe di akaretsa sekolašipi sa dikgwedi di le tharo kwa Amerika koo Rre Hendricks a tla ithutang kwa Philadelphia Orchestra mme a katisiwa ke Moporofesara Victor Yampolsky kwa Chicago.

src: Cabinet congratulates film producer, Mr Anant Singh, for being awarded third place for the film Shepherds and Butchers in the Panorama Audience Award for Fiction Film at the Berlin International Film Festival.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola motlhagisi wa difilimi, Rre Anant Singh, ka ntlha ya go abelwa maemo a boraro ka filimi ya Shepherds and Butchers kwa Panorama Audience Award for Fiction Film kwa Moletlong wa Boditšhabatšhaba wa Difilimi wa Berlin.

src: This is a major achievement as the film competed against 51 feature-length films from 33 countries.
tgt: Seno ke phitlhelelo e kgolo ka ntlha ya fa filimi e ne e gaisana le difilimi di le 51 go tswa kwa dinageng di le Go thapiwaGo thapiwa gotlhe go tla diragadiwa fa makwalothuto otlhe a netefaditswe mme go amogetswe tetlelelo e e matshwanedi:.

src: Extension of the contract for Mr Lionel October as the Director-General (DG) in the Department of Trade and Industry, for a period of five years.
tgt: Katoloso ya konteraka ya ga Rre Lionel October jaaka Mokaedikakaretso (DG) mo Lefapheng la Kgwebisano le Indaseteri, sebaka sa dingwaga di le tlhano.

src: Appointment of Dr Mantlhake J Maboya as the Deputy DG (DDG): Curriculum Policy and Monitoring in the Department of Basic Education.
tgt: Go thapiwa ga Ngaka Mantlhake J Maboya jaaka Motlatsamokaedikakaretso (DDG): Pholisi ya Kharikhulamo le Tekolo mo Lefapheng la Thuto ya Motheo.

src: Appointment of Ms Shamilla Chettiar as the DDG: Policy and Knowledge Services in the Department of Tourism.
tgt: Go thapiwa ga Mme Shamilla Chettiar jaaka DDG: Ditirelo tsa Pholisi le Kitso kwa Lefapheng la Bojanala.

src: Appointment of Mr Mbulelo Tshangana as the DG in the Department of Human Settlements.
tgt: Go thapiwa ga Rre Mbulelo Tshangana jaaka DG mo Lefapheng la Manno a Batho.

src: Reappointment of Mr Kutoane Obed Kutoane as the Chief Executive Officer of the Export Credit Insurance Corporation of South Africa SOC Limited.
tgt: Go thapiwa gape ga Rre Kutoane Obed Kutoane jaaka Motlhankedikhuduthamagamogolo wa Export Credit Insurance Corporation of South Africa SOC Limited.

src: Cabinet assessed the Third Quarter Outcomes Progress Reports for the period October to December 2015.
tgt: Kabinete e sekasekile Dipegelo tsa Dipoelo tsa Dikgatelopele tsa Kotara ya Boraro tsa paka ya Diphalane go fitlha Sedimonthole 2015.

src: The reports show significant progress in the implementation of government programmes that have a direct impact on improving the lives of South Africans.
tgt: Dipegelo di bontsha kgatelopele e e utlwalang malebana le go tsenngwa tirisong ga manaane a puso a a amang ka tlhamalalo tokafatso ya matshelo a maAforika Borwa.

src: The Outcomes Progress Reports provide evidence that government has made progress in achieving the targets set out in the Medium Term Strategic Framework 2014-2019.
tgt: Dipegelo tsa Dipoelo tsa Dikgatelopele di naya bosupi jwa gore puso e dirile kgatelopele go fitlhelela diphitlhelelo tse di neng di tlhagisitswe mo Letlhomesong la Togamaano ya Pakagare la 2014-2019.

src: They also take us closer to realising Vision 2030, as articulated in the National Development Plan, which aims to tackle poverty, unemployment and inequality.
tgt: Gape di re atametsa le go fitlhelela Ponelopele ya 2030 jaaka e tlhagisitswe mo Leano la Tlhabololo la Bosetšhaba (NDP), le maitlhomo a lona e leng go samagana le lehuma, botlhokatiro le go tlhoka tekatekano.

src: Cabinet noted the reasonable progress that was made to achieve the key targets and outputs.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile tswelelopele e e amogelesegang e e dirilweng go fitlhelela diphitlhelelo le ditlhagiso tsa botlhokwa.

src: Cabinet has noted that while significant progress was made in respect of most of the indicators, there are still areas that require coordinated interventions by government.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile gore le fa go nnile le tswelelopele e e bonalang malebana le bontsi jwa disupi, go sa ntse go na le dikarolo tse di tlhokang tsereganyo e e gokaganeng ya puso.

src: Implementation of key government programmes.
tgt: Go tsenngwa tirisong ga manaane a botlhokwa a puso.

src: Cabinet has expressed its gratitude to all South Africans who responded to the call by the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) for people to register, check their registration status and update their details on the voters’ roll on the weekend of 5 and 6 March 2016.
tgt: Kabinete e tlhagisitse Ditebogo tsa yona go maAforika Borwa a a tsibogetseng boikuelo jwa Khomišene ya Ditlhopho e e Ikemetseng (IEC) jwa gore batho ba ikwadise, ba tlhole seemo sa bone sa ikwadiso mmogo le go ntšhwafatsa dintlha tsa bona mo lenaneng la batlhopi ka mafelo a beke a la bo 5 le la bo 6 Mopitlwe 2016.

src: About three million people visited polling stations countrywide and 544 552 of the new registrations (78.6%) were under the age of 30, which demonstrates the willingness by South Africans to participate in building our democracy.
tgt: Batho ba ka nna dimilione di le tharo ba etetse diteišene tsa ditlhopho naga ka bophara mme baikwadisi ba bantšhwa ba le 544 552 (78%) ba ne ba le dingwaga tse di ka fa tlase ga 30, e leng sesupo sa keletso ya maAforika Borwa go nna le seabe mo go ageng temokerasi ya rona.

src: Cabinet calls on South Africans to exercise their democratic right by registering and urges those who have registered previously to verify their voter registration details as a number of factors have led to changes in the voters’ roll.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo maAforika Borweng go diragatsa tshwanelo ya bona ya molaotheo ka go ikwadisa mme e rotloetsa ba ba ikwadisitseng mo nakong e e fetileng go tlhomamisa dintlha tsa bona tsa ikwadiso ya ditlhopho ka ntlha ya fa go na le mabaka a le mmalwa a a bakileng diphetogo mo lenaneng la batlhopi.

src: The final registration weekend will take place on 9 and 10 April 2016 when all voting stations will again be open from 8:00 to 17:00.
tgt: Beke ya bofelo ya ikwadiso e tla nna ka la bo 9 le la bo 10 Moranang 2016 fa diteišene tsa ditlhopho di tla bo di butswe gape go tloga ka ura ya bo 8:00 mo mosong go fitlha ka ura ya bo 17:00 mo maetsiboeng.

src: This will be the last opportunity for voters to register and update their registration details at their voting stations.
tgt: Seno e tla bo e le tšhono ya bofelo ya gore batlhophi ba ikwadise le go ntšhwafatsa dintlha tsa bona tsa ikwadiso kwa diteišene tsa ditlhopho.

src: However, registration is ongoing at local IEC offices during office hours from Monday to Friday, until the voters’ roll for the 2016 Municipal Elections closes on the day the elections are promulgated.
tgt: Le fa go le jalo, go ikwadisa go tswelela pele kwa dikantorong tsa selegae tsa IEC ka dinako tsa tiro go tloga Mosupologo go fitlha ka Labotlhano, go fitlha lenane la batlhophi la Ditlhopho tsa Makgotlatoropo tsa 2016 le tswalelwa ka letsatsi le go tla bong go itsesiwe letlha la ditlhopho ka lona.

src: Cabinet condemns the violence in some areas that marred the recent registration weekend and reiterates that no person may prevent any South African from exercising their democratic right to register to vote.
tgt: Kabinete e kgalema ka bogale tirisodikgoka e e neng e aparetse mafelo a beke ya ikwadiso fa gautshwane kwa mafelong mangwe mme e boeletsa gore ga gona motho ope yo o tshwanetseng go thibela moAforika Borwa ope go diragatsa tshwanelo ya gagwe ya tmolaotheo ya go ikwadisetsa go tlhopha.

src: Cabinet further calls on all those responsible to desist from such criminal activities and for those affected to report them to law-enforcement agencies.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela gape mo go botlhe ba ba rweleng maikarabelo go tila dikgato tseo tsa bosenyi le gore ba ba amegang ba bege ditiragalo tseo kwa ditheong tsa tiragatso ya molao.

src: Cabinet calls on all law-enforcement agencies to take strong action against law-breakers.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo ditheong tsotlhe tsa tiragatso ya molao go tsaya dikgato tse di bogale kgatlhanong le batlolamolao.

src: President Jacob Zuma will visit Port Elizabeth on 8 April 2016 to inspect progress made in developing marine transport infrastructure as part of the country’s Oceans Economy initiative.
tgt: Moporesitente Jacob Zuma o tla etela Port Elizabeth ka la bo 8 Moranang 2016 go tlhatlhoba kgatelopele e e dirilweng tebang le go tlhabolola mafaratlhatlha a dipalangwa tsa mo lewatleng jaaka karolo ya maiteko a naga a Ikonomi ya Lewatle.

src: The Oceans Economy is one of the three streams of Operation Phakisa and takes the country closer to unlocking the potential of South Africa’s oceans, which has the potential to contribute up to R177 billion to the gross domestic product and create over one million new jobs.
tgt: Ikonomi ya Lewatle ke nngwe ya maphata a le mararo a Operation Phakisa mme e atametsa naga gaufi le go bula bokgoni jwa mawatle a Aforika Borwa, a a nang le bokgoni jwa go nna le seabe sa bokana ka R177 bilione mo ikonoming ya naga le go tlhama ditiro tse dintšhwa di feta milione.

src: Cabinet welcomes the successful conclusion of the State Visit by President Zuma to the Federal Republic of Nigeria from 8 to 9 March 2016, which enhanced existing bilateral political, economic and social ties.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela go konosediwa ka katlego ga Leeto la Semmuso la ga Moporesitente Zuma kwa Rephaboliking ya Bofeterale ya Nigeria go tloga ka la bo 8 go fitlha ka la bo 9 Mopitlwe 2016, e e tokafaditseng dikgolagano tse di leng gona tsa sebedi tsa sepolotiki, ikonomi le loago.

src: One of the milestones of the visit was the elevation of the Binational Commission to a Head of State level, which prioritises economic development between the two countries.
tgt: Nngwe ya dintlhakgolo tsa diphitlhelelo tsa leeto e nnile go godisiwa ga Khomišene ya Dinagapedi go ya kwa seemong sa Tlhogo ya Mmuso, e leng se se bayang tlhabololo ya ikonomi magareng ga dinaga tse pedi go nna setlapele.

src: Cabinet welcomes the opening of Nigeria’s economy to South African companies in various sectors such as engineering, telecommunications, construction, aviation, media, hospitality, banking, entertainment, property, retail, and oil and gas exploration services.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela go bulelwa ga ikonomi ya Nigeria ditlamo tsa Aforika Borwa mo maphateng a a farologaneng a tshwana le a boenjiniri, ditlhaeletsano tsa megala, dikago, diphofo, bobegakgang, bojanala, dibanka, boitumediso, dithoto, kgwebo, mmogo le ditirelo tsa go phuruphutsha oli le gase.

src: Cabinet looks forward to the increase in the number of Nigerian investments in South Africa that will promote two-way trade between the two nations.
tgt: Kabinete e letetse kgolo ya palo ya dipeeletso tsa Nigeria mo Aforika Borwa e leng se se tla tsweletsang kgwebisano ya maphatamabedi magareng ga dinaga tse pedi tse.

src: The outcomes from this engagement between two of the largest economies on the continent will integrate regional economies, thereby increasing the common market and elevating existing initiatives of economic growth and employment in Africa.
tgt: Dipoelo tsa puisano eno magareng ga diikonomi tse pedi tse dikgolo go gaisa mo kontinenteng di tla gokaganya diikonomi tsa kgaolo, mme ka go rialo di oketse mmaraka o o tlhakanetsweng le go godisa maiteko a a leng teng a kgolo ya ikonomi mmogo le ditiro mo Aforika.

src: This demonstrates that South Africa remains a competitive investment destination despite a troubled global economy, and will result in job opportunities and skills development for South Africans.
tgt: Seno se supa gore Aforika Borwa e sa ntse e le boyo jo bo gaisanang jwa dipeeletso le fa ikonomi ya lefatshe e ntse e le mo mathateng, mme se tla lebisa kwa ditšhonong tsa ditiro mmogo le tlhabololo ya bokgoni jwa maAforika Borwa otlhe.

src: Cabinet noted that South Africa will be participating at the 60th Session of the United Nations (UN) Commission on the Status of Women (CSW60) taking place in New York, USA from 14 to 24 March 2016 under the theme: “Women’s empowerment and its link to sustainable development”.
tgt: Kabinete e tsibogetse gore Aforika Borwa e tla nna le seabe mo Kopanong ya bo 60 ya Khomišene ya Seemo sa Basadi ya Ditšhabakopano (UN) (CSW60) e e diragalang kwa New York, Amerika go tloga ka la bo 14 go fitlha ka la bo 24 Mopitlwe 2016 ka fa tlase ga moono wa: “Maatlafatso ya basadi le kgolagano ya yona le tlhabololo e e nnelang leruri.” Kopano e diragala mo ngwageng wa botlhokwa wa Aforika Borwa ka ntlha ya fa o na le diphitlhelelo tse tharo tsa botlhokwa, e leng, Segopotso sa bo 20 sa Molaotheo wa Rephaboliki ya Aforika Borwa wa 1996, Segopotso sa bo 40 sa Dikhuduego tsa kwa Soweto le Segopotso sa bo 60 sa mogwanto wa basadi wa 1956.Aforika Borwa e tlhagisitse pegelo kwa UN CSW60 mme seno se re naya tšhono ya go lekanyetsa kgatelopele e re e dirileng fa e sale re bona temokerasi.

src: The session is taking place in an important year for South Africa as it marks three important milestones, namely the 20th Anniversary of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996, 40th Anniversary of the Soweto Youth Uprising and the 60th Anniversary of the 1956 women’s march.
tgt: Go botlhokwa go lemoga gore fa e sale ka puso ya temokerasi, Aforika Borwa, gareng ga tse dingwe, e nnile le seabe kwa Khonferenseng ya bo 4 ya Lefatshe ya Basadi ka 1995, mme ya saena Sekwalwa sa Beijing sa Maikano le Dirala tsa go tsaya Dikgato gone mo ngwageng oo.

src: South Africa has presented a report to the UN CSW60 and this gives us an opportunity to benchmark the progress we have made since the dawn of democracy.
tgt: Go lepalepana le tshwetso ya E/RES/2013/18 ya Lekgotla la UN la Ikonomi le Loago, Aforika Borwa e itlamile go tswelela go diragatsa Sekwalwa sa Beijing sa Maikano le Dirala tsa go tsaya Dikgato, e leng leano la maatlafatso le tsweletso ya basadi.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Local Government: Municipal Structures Amendment Bill of 2016 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e amogetse go tlhagisiwa ga Molaotlhomo o o Baakantsweng wa Dipopegotheo tsa Makgotlatoropo wa 2016 wa Pusoselegae kwa Palamenteng.

src: Amendments are being made to the Local Government: Municipal Structures Act, 1998 (Act 117 of 1998), which was enacted prior to the first democratic local government elections which took place on 5 December 2000.The amendments will improve the administration of local government elections and among other changes, seek to:a) amend criteria for Category A municipalitiesb) remove all references to district management areasc) clarify the date of assumption of office by a councillord) determine the President must set and call the date for the municipal electionse) allow for extension in the declaration of results of an electionf) require a municipal manager to inform the IEC of ward vacanciesg) determine that a Member of the Executive Council calls and sets the date for by-electionsh) clarify the quorum requirements for a council meetingi) clarify the circumstances for the casting vote of a councillor presiding during a council meetingj) increase variance of the number of voters in each ward during a council meeting andk) increase variance of the number of voters in each ward during a demarcation to clarify the allocation of excessive seats in local municipalities.
tgt: Go dirwa dipaakanyo mo Molaong wa Dipopegotheo tsa Makgotlatoropo,1998 (Molao wa bo 117 wa 1998) wa Pusoselegae o o fetisitsweng pele ga ditlhopho tsa ntlha tsa temokerasi tsa pusoselegae tse di diragetseng ka la bo 5 Sedimonthole 2000.Dipaakanyo di tla tokafatsa tsamaiso ya ditlhopho tsa pusoselegae mme gareng ga diphetogo tse dingwe, o batla go:a) baakanya seemo sa makgotlatoropo a Karolo ya Ab) tlosa go kaiwa ga dikarolo tsa tsamaiso ya dikgaoloc) tlhamalatsa letlha la go simolola tiro ga molekgotlad) letla Moporesitente go tlhoma le go itsise letlha la ditlhopho tsa makgotlatoropoe) letla gore go nne le katoloso ya kitsiso ya dipholo tsa ditlhophof) gore motsamaisi wa lekgotlatoropo a itsese IEC ka diphatlhatiro tse di mo otongg) swetsa gore Mokhuduthamaga a itsise le go tlhoma letlha la ditlhopho tsa tlaleletsoh) tlhamalatsa ditlhokego tsa maloko a setlhophatshwetso tsa kopano ya lekgotlai) tlhamalatsa mabaka a go tlhopha ga molekgotla yo e leng modulasetilo ka nako ya kopano ya lekgotlaj) oketsa pharologano ya palo ya batlhophi mo otong nngwe le nngwe ka nako ya kopano ya lekgotla lek) oketsa pharologano ya palo ya batlhophi mo otong nngwe le nngwe ka nako ya go aroganngwa ga melelwane go tlhalosa kabo ya ditilo tse di fetang tekano mo makgotlatoropong a selegae.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Ditiragalo tse di tlang.

src: President Zuma – as co-chair with French President François Hollande of the High-Level Commission on Health Employment and Economic Growth – will attend its formal launch in Lyon, France on Wednesday, 23 March 2016.
tgt: Moporesitente Zuma - jaaka modulasetilommogo le Moporesitente wa Fora François Hollande wa Khomišene ya Maemo a a Kwa Godimo ya Ditiro tsa Boitekanelo le Kgolo ya Ikonomi - o tla tsenela go tlhomiwa ga yona semmuso kwa Lyon, Fora ka Laboraro, 23 Mopitlwe 2016.

src: The commission focuses on the need for health professionals in middle and low-income countries.
tgt: Khomišene e totile tlhokego ya baporofešenale ba boitekanelo mo dinageng tsa lotseno lo lo magareng le lo lo kwa tlase.

src: This UN initiative is expected to increase health security worldwide and promote inclusive economic growth, which contributes to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
tgt: Go solofetswe gore maiteko ano a UN a oketse go nna teng ga boitekanelo lefatshe ka bophara le go tsweletsa kgolo ya ikonomi e e akaretsang, e e nang le seabe mo tiragatsong ya Lenaane la 2030 la Tlhabololo e e nnelang Leruri.

src: President Zuma will undertake a State Visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia from 27 to 28 March 2016, which will strengthen existing relations between the two countries.
tgt: Moporesident Zuma o tla tsaya Leeto la Semmuso go ya kwa Nagabogosing ya Saudi Arabia go tloga ka la bo 27 go fitlha ka la bo 28 Mopitlwe 2016, le le tla maatlafatsang botsalano jo bo leng teng magareng ga dinaga tse pedi.

src: The President will attend the 4th Nuclear Security Summit in Washington, USA from 31 March to 1 April 2016.
tgt: Moporesitente o tla tsenela Samiti ya bo 4 ya Tshireletsego ya Nyutlilea kwa Washington, Amerika go tloga ka la bo 31 Mopitlwe go fitlha ka la bo 1 Moranang 2016.

src: The summit will discuss the evolving threat of nuclear terrorism and highlight steps that can be taken by the international community to minimise the use of highly enriched uranium, secure vulnerable materials, counter nuclear smuggling and deter, detect and disrupt attempts at nuclear terrorism.
tgt: Samiti e tla bua ka matshosetsi a a golang a borukhutli jwa nyutlilea le go sedimosa dikgato tse di ka tsewang ke baagi ba boditšhabatšhaba go fokotsa tiriso ya yuraniamo e e humileng thata, go sireletsa dimateriale tse di mo matshosetsing, go tsibogela go utswiwa ga nyutlilea le go thibela, batlisisa le go kgoreletsa maiteko a borukhutli jwa nyutlilea.

src: President Zuma will lead Human Rights Day celebrations at the Moses Mabhida Stadium in KwaZulu-Natal on Monday, 21 March 2016 under the theme: “South Africa united against racism.” As announced in the 2016 State of the Nation Address, this year’s Human Rights Day will lay the foundation for a long-term programme of building a non-racial society.
tgt: Moporesitente Zuma o tla etelela pele meletlo ya Letsatsi la Ditshwanelo tsa Botho kwa Setediamo sa Moses Mabhida kwa KwaZulu-Natal ka Mosupologo, 21 Mopitlwe ka fa tlase ga moono wa: "Aforika Borwa e kopane kgatlhanong le bosemorafe."

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to unite against and denounce racism – be it in our homes, communities, social gatherings, workplaces or on social media.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo maAforika Borweng otlhe go kopana kgatlhanong le, le go nyatsa bosemorafe - e ka nna kwa magaeng a rona, mo baaging, mo dikopanong tsa loago, kwa ditirong gongwe mo mafaratlhatlheng a ditlhaeletsano tsa loago.

src: We must all work together to achieve a united, non-racial and non-sexist democracy.
tgt: Re tshwanetse go dira mmogo go fitlhelela temokerasi e e kopaneng, e e sa tlhaoleng go ya ka bosemorafe le fa e le go tlhaola go ya ka bong.

src: Members of the Executive will interact with South Africans across the country during the National Imbizo Focus Week between 4 and 10 April 2016, under the theme: “Together we move South Africa forward: Grow South Africa.” The week coincides with the Parliamentary Constituency Week and the commemoration of Freedom Month.
tgt: Bakhuduthamaga ba tla buisana le maAforika Borwa go ralala naga ka nako ya Beke ya Bosetšhaba ya Imbizo magareng ga la bo 4 le la bo 10 Moranang 2016, ka fa tlase ga moono wa: Mmogo re tsweletsa pele Aforika Borwa: Godisa Aforika Borwa."

src: Cabinet encourages South Africans to actively participate in these events and to engage with political principals.
tgt: Kabinete e rotloetsa maAforika Borwa go nna le seabe se se tlhaga mo ditiragalong tseno le go buisana le baeteledipele ba sepolotiki.

src: The Imbizo Focus Week will highlight the implementation of the Nine-Point Plan that aims to boost economic growth and create much-needed jobs.
tgt: Beke ya Imbizo e tla tlhagisa go tsenngwa tirisong ga Leano la Dintlharobongwe le maikaelelo a lona e leng go susumetsa kgolo ya ikonomi le go tlhama ditiro tse di tlhokegang thata.

src: It will also profile local government successes, including achievements yielded through the local government revitalisation plan – the Back-to-Basics approach.
tgt: E tla bontsha gape dikatlego tsa pusoselegae, go akarediwa diphitlhelelo tse di fitlheletsweng ka ntlha ya leano la tsosoloso ya pusoselegae - dikgato tsa Re boela kwa Tshimologong.

src: The week will also coincide with the final registration weekend ahead of the 2016 Municipal Elections, further providing an opportunity for principals to galvanise and mobilise South Africans through voter education outreaches to register and verify their voting details.
tgt: Gape beke eo e tla tsamaelana le mafelo a beke a ikwadiso ya bofelo pele ga Ditlhopho tsa Makgotlatoropo tsa 2016, e naya gape baeteledipele tšhono ya go susumetsa le go rotloetsa maAforika Borwa ka thuto ya ditlhopho go ikwadisa le go tlhomamisa dintlha tsa bona tsa go tlhopha.

src: Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa will open the 2nd Human Resource Development Council Summit taking place at the Gallagher Convention Centre in Midrand on 29 and 30 March 2016 under the theme: “Partnership for skills – A Call to Action”.
tgt: Motlatsamoporesitente Cyril Ramaphosa o tla bula Samiti ya bo 2 ya Lekgotla la Tlhabololo ya Badiri e e tla diragalang kwa Gallagher Convention Centre kwa Midrand ka la bo 29 le la bo 30 Mopitlwe 2016, ka fa tlase ga moono wa: "Tirisanommogo go lebeletswe bokgoni - Boikuelo jwa go tsaya Dikgato".

src: The summit brings together stakeholders from across the higher education sector to assist in its development and forge partnerships that create stronger industry-ready higher education institutions.
tgt: Samiti e kgobokanya baamegi go tswa kwa lephateng la thuto e kgolwane go thusa mo tlhabololong ya lona le go tlhama tirisanommogo e e tla bopang ditheo tsa thuto e e kgolwane tse di maatla e bile di siametse indaseteri.

src: National Water Week 2016 will take place from 14 to 22 March under the theme: “Water for people, water by people”.
tgt: Beke ya Bosetšhaba ya Metsi ya 2016 e tla ketekiwa go tloga ka la bo 14 go fitlha ka la bo 22 Mopitlwe ka moono wa: "Metsi a batho, metsi ka batho".

src: The week will profile water as a human right by raising awareness of the plight of people who do not have access to clean drinkable water.
tgt: Beke e tla tlhagisa metsi jaaka tshwanelo ya botho ka go godisa temogo ya mathata a batho ba ba sa kgoneng go fitlhelela metsi a a phepa, a a nwegang.

src: The Department of Water and Sanitation is still in the process of eradicating the bucket system and has thus far eradicated 78.8% of the bucket system in formal settlements in South Africa.
tgt: Lefapha la Metsi le Kgeleloleswe le sa ntse le tsweletse ka go fedisa thulaganyo ya matlwana a dikgamelo mme ga jaana le setse le fedisitse 78% ya thulaganyo ya matlwana a dikgamelo kwa mafelong a baipei mo Aforika Borwa.

src: Seven provinces have performed excellently with an average 90% eradication.
tgt: Diporofense di le supa di dirile bontle tota ka palogare ya phediso ya 90%.

src: Those that have achieved total eradication in formal settlements are KwaZulu-Natal, North West, Mpumalanga and Gauteng.
tgt: Tse di kgonneng go fedisa gotlhelele kwa mafelong a baipei ke KwaZulu-Natal, Bokone Bophirima, Mpumalanga le Gauteng.

src: The Western Cape has reached 99.8% clearance.
tgt: Kapa Bophirima e fitlheletse 99.8%.

src: From a target of 26 120 for the Northern Cape, Eastern Cape, North West and Free State, some 11 650 systems have been completed to date.
tgt: Go tswa mo diphitlhelelong tse di neng di beilwe tsa 26 120 kwa Kapa Bokone, Kapa Botlhaba, Bokone Bophirima le Foreisetata, go konoseditswe dithulaganyo di le 11 650 go fitlha ga jaana.

src: While the recent rainfall brought some relief, the impact of the drought continues to be felt in some parts of the country.
tgt: Le fa pula ya fa gautshwane e thusitse, ditlamorago tsa komelelo di tsweletse go utlwala mo dikarolong dingwe tsa naga.

src: South Africans must continue to use water sparingly and implement water-saving initiatives.
tgt: MaAforika Borwa a tshwanetse go tswelela go somarela metsi le go diragatsa maiteko a go a boloka.

src: Government has since provided R1 billion to deal with the drought crisis.
tgt: Puso e tlametse ka R1 bilione go samagana le mathata a komelelo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the progress being made by the five-year War on Leaks programme under the theme: “Every drop counts”.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela tswelelopele e e dirilweng ke lenaane la Ntwa kgatlhanong le go dutla ga dipeipi tsa metsi ka fa tlase ga moono wa: "Lerothodi lengwe le lengwe le botlhokwa".

src: The programme aims to recruit, train and deploy 15 000 young people with the minimum qualification of Grade 12 or N3 as plumbers, artisans and water agents.
tgt: Lenaane le ikaelela go ngoka, katisa le go phasalatsa bašwa ba le 15 000 ba ba nang le dithuto tse dinnye tsa Mophato wa 12 gongwe N3 jaaka dipolamara, diathisene gongwe baemedi ba metsi.

src: Cabinet’s position on key issues in the environment.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete mo Mererong e e Botlhokwa ya ga jaana.

src: Cabinet appeals to protesters to act with the utmost restraint and express their grievances within the confines of the law and the Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela go badiraditshupetso go itshwara le go tlhagisa dingongorego tsa bona ka tsela e e obamelang molao le Molaotheo.

src: Vandalism and damage of property goes beyond the limits of the right to protest and is the work of misguided criminal elements.
tgt: Go thuba le go senya dithoto ga e tlhole e le tshwanelo ya go dira ditshupetso mme ke tiro ya disenyi tse di senang taolo.

src: Law-enforcement agencies will uphold the law by apprehending and charging those who destroy property at universities, other institutions of higher learning, in communities and during protest action.
tgt: Ditheo tsa tiragatso ya molao di tla diragatsa molao ka go tshwara le go pega molato ba ba senyang dithoto kwa diyunibesithi, ditheong tse dingwe tsa thuto e kgolwane, le mo baaging ka nako ya ditshupetso.

src: The Minister of Finance briefed Cabinet on the recent roadshows that he undertook to the US and United Kingdom with various stakeholders, including business leaders.
tgt: Tona ya Ditšhelete o begetse Kabinete ka letsholo la fa gautshwane le a le tsereng go ya Amerika le Borithane le baamegi ba ba farologaneng, go akarediwa baeteledipele ba kgwebo.

src: Cabinet is committed to ensuring that the country works together to ensure that we are not downgraded.
tgt: Kabinete e itlamile go netefatsa gore naga e dira mmogo go netefatsa gore maemo a rona ga a fokodiwe.

src: The visit offers government the opportunity to share a number of initiatives implemented to deal with challenges.
tgt: Leeto leno le naya puso tšhono ya go tlhalosa ka maiteko a le mmalwa a a diragadiwang go samagana le dikgwetlho.

src: These include collaborative actions to accelerate inclusive growth, measures to fast-track fiscal consolidation, speed up implementation of our R870 billion Infrastructure Investment Programme and progress made in resolving the energy constraints, including through renewable energy.
tgt: Ona a akaretsa dikgato tse di tshwaraganetsweng go akofisa kgolo e e akaretsang botlhe, dikgato tsa go akofisa tsolotanyo ya ditšhelete, go akofisa go tsenngwa tirisong ga Lenaane la Dipeeletso tsa Mafaratlhatlha la R870 bilione mmogo le tswelelopele e e dirilweng go rarabolola mathata a motlakase, go akarediwa motlakase o o ntšhwafadiwang.

src: Cabinet calls on all sectors to communicate all the positive programmes and interventions undertaken to safeguard our economy.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo maphateng otlhe go buisanela manaane le ditsereganyo tse di tserweng go sireletsa ikonomi ya rona.

src: It is important for all sectors to ensure that the country’s economy is resilient.
tgt: Go botlhokwa gore maphata otlhe a netefatse gore ikonomi ya naga e kgona go emelana le dikgwetlho.

src: In this regard, Cabinet has also instructed the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Investment to fast track all key economic-related decisions.
tgt: Mo ntlheng eno, Kabinete e laetse gape Komiti ya Ditona ya Dipeeletso go akofisa ditshwetso tsotlhe tsa botlhokwa tse di amanang le ikonomi.

src: Cabinet reiterates that the resilience of the South African economy is built on sound economic fundamentals and practical policies.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa gore go emelana le dikgwetlho ga ikonomi ya Aforika Borwa go agilwe mo dintlhatheong tse di tsepameng tsa ikonomi mmogo le dipholisi tse di dirisegang.

src: Cabinet noted a court case brought by the Chamber of Mines for the Mining Charter to be declared unconstitutional and void.
tgt: Kabinete e lemogile kgetse ya kgotlatshekelo e e tlhatlhetsweng ke Mokgatlho wa Meepo ya gore Tumelano ya Meepo e se e e mo molaotheong mme e tseewe jaaka e e seng mosola.

src: Cabinet reiterates that the principles of the Mining Charter are aimed at transforming the mining industry to redress historical imbalances engendered by apartheid so that the industry is consistent with the changes in South Africa’s overall transformation of its social, political and economic landscape.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa gore dintlhatheo tsa Tumelano ya Meepo di ikaeletse go fetola indaseteri ya meepo le go samagana le go tlhoka tekatekano ga maloba go go tlhotlheleditsweng ke tlhaolele gore indaseteri e lepalepane le diphetogo tsa go fetolwa ka kakaretso ga seemo sa Aforika Borwa sa loago, polotiki mmogo le ikonomi.

src: Community upliftment is also a key focus area to ensure that mining development does not exclude relevant communities.
tgt: Kgodiso ya baagi ke ntlha e nngwe ya botlhokwa go netefatsa gore tlhabololo ya meepo ga e kgaphele thoko baagi ba ba maleba.

src: Cabinet calls on all road users, especially those travelling over the upcoming holiday period, to play their part by taking responsibility for their own safety and that of other road users.
tgt: Kabinete e ikuela mo badirising botlhe ba tsela, bogolo segolo ba ba tla bong ba le mo maetong ka paka ya malatsi a boikhutso, go diragatsa seabe sa bona ka go rwala maikarabelo a pabalesego ya bona le ya badirisi ba bangwe ba tsela.

src: Ending the road carnage remains a national priority.
tgt: Go fedisa matlhotlhapelo a mo tseleng e sa ntse e le setlapele sa bosetšhaba.

src: Drivers must be alert, obey the rules of the road, not drink and drive, keep to the speed limit and ensure that their vehicles are roadworthy.
tgt: Bakgweetsi ba tshwanetse go nna ba butse matlho, ba obamele melawana ya tsela, ba seke ba nwa mme ba kgweetsa, ba obamele tekanyetso ya lebelo mmogo le go netefatsa gore dijanaga tsa bona di siametse tsela.

src: Cabinet congratulates all the winners of the National Disability Rights Awards held on 11 March 2016.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola bafenyi botlhe ba Dikgele tsa Bosetšhaba tsa Ditshwanelo tsa Bogole tse di neng di tshwerwe ka la bo 11 Mopitlwe 2016.

src: These awards recognised persons with disabilities and disability rights activists who have excelled during 2015.
tgt: Dikgele tseno di lemogile batho ba ba nang le bogole le balweladitshwanelo ba ditshwanelo tsa bogole ba ba itshupileng ka 2015.

src: Cabinet salutes all the winners of the 3rd South African Police Service (SAPS) Annual National Excellence Awards, which pay tribute to excellence by SAPS members, reservists and members of community police forums.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola bafenyi botlhe ba Dikgele tsa bo 3 tsa Bosetšhaba tsa Botswerere tsa Ngwaga le Ngwaga tsa Tirelo ya Sepodisi sa Aforika Borwa (SAPS), tse di akgolang botswerere jwa ditokololo tsa SAPS, maresefe mmogo le ditokololo tsa diforamo tsa baagi tsa sepodisi.

src: Cabinet applauds co-writers Mandla Dube and Leon Otto of Pambili Media for the film Kalushi: The Story of Solomon Mahlangu.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola bakwadimmogo Mandla Dube le Leon Otto ba Pambili Media ka baesekopo ya bona ya Kalushi: The Story of Solomon Mahlangu.

src: South Africans are encouraged to watch this political thriller about the transformation of a 19-year-old young man from Mamelodi, east of Pretoria, into a Struggle icon.
tgt: MaAforika Borwa a rotloediwa go bogela baesekopo eno ya sepolotiki e e kgatlhisang e e ka ga go fetoga ga mosimanyana wa dingwaga di le 19 wa kwa Mamelodi, kwa botlhaba jwa Pretoria, go nna mogaka wa Kgaratlho.

src: Cabinet reiterated that government will, through the departments of Trade and Industry and Arts and Culture, continue to support the growth of the arts industry in celebrating and telling the South African story.
tgt: Kabinete e boeleditse gore puso, ka Lefapha la Kgwebisano le Indaseteri le la Botsweretshi le Setso, e tla tswelela go tshegetsa kgolo ya indaseteri ya botsweretshi ka go keteka le go anela dikgang tsa Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet congratulates social justice activist Father Michael Lapsley for receiving the international 2016 Public Peace Prize in the category ‘Global Peace and Reconciliation – Internationally-Reputed Peacemaker’.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola molweladitshwanelo tsa bosiamisi jwa loago Moruti Michael Lapsey ka go amogela Sekgele sa Kagiso ya Setšhaba sa boditšhabatšhaba sa 2016 mo karolong ya 'Kagiso ya Lefatshe le Poelano - Modirakagiso yo o Itsegeng Boditšhabatšhaba'.

src: Cabinet applauds Pieter du Preez for being nominated for the Laureus World Sportsperson of the Year with a Disability Award, following his outstanding performances in 2015.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola Pieter du Preez jaaka a tlhophetswe Sekgele sa Motshameki wa Lefatshe wa Ngwaga yo o nang le Bogole sa Laureus, go latela tiragatso ya gagwe e e gaisitseng ka 2015.

src: Cabinet congratulates Wayde van Niekerk who made sprinting history by becoming the first man in history to run all three races: the 100m in under 10 seconds‚ the 200m in under 20 seconds and the 400m in under 44 seconds‚ as confirmed by the International Association of Athletics Federations.
tgt: Kabinete e akgola Wayde van Niekerk yo o dirileng hisetori ya lebelo ka go nna monna wa ntlha mo hisetoring go taboga mabelo otlhe a le mararo: 100m ka fa tlase ga metsotswana e le 10, 200m ka fa tlase ga metsotswana e le 20 le 400m ka fa tlase ga metsotswana e le 44, jaaka go tlhomamisitswe ke Mokgatlho wa Boditšhabatšhaba wa Difetereišene tsa Mabelo.

src: Implementation of key government programmes.
tgt: Go tsenngwa tirisong ga manaane a botlhokwa a puso.

src: Cabinet welcomes the achievements highlighted by President Jacob Zuma during his site visit to the Port of Port Elizabeth in the Eastern Cape, to assess progress made on the implementation of the Operation Phakisa: Oceans Economy initiative.
tgt: Kabinete e amogela diphitlhelelo tse di tlhagisitsweng ke Moporesitente Jacob Zuma ka nako ya ketelo ya setsha kwa Boemelakepeng jwa Port Elizabeth kwa Kapa Botlhaba, go sekaseka kgatelopele e e leng teng malebana le go tsenngwa tirisong ga Operation Phakisa: e leng maiteko a Ikonomi ya Mawatle.

src: Government has unlocked investments amounting to about R17 billion in the Oceans Economy.
tgt: Puso e golotse dipeeletso tse di ka nnang bokana ka R17 bilione mo Ikonoming ya Mawatle.

src: Since its inception, over 4 500 jobs have been created in various sectors.
